utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Registrar, can you kindly call the case, please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. Good morning, Your Honours. Good morning to everyone in and around the courtroom. This is case number IT-04-74-T, the Prosecutor versus Jadranko Prlic et al. Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Registrar. Today is Monday. I would like to greet Mr. Tomic, first of all, who stayed here for a few days, waiting for the hearing to resume. I would like to thank him. I would like to greet the accused, the counsel, Mr. Scott and Mr. Kruger, as well as their associate, and all the people helping us in this courtroom. We are today going to begin the cross-examination. Since we have very little time, I shall not waste any more time and give the floor to Mr. Scott straight away.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Good afternoon to Your Honours, each of you, and good afternoon to all those in and around the courtroom, Counsel, and good afternoon, Mr. Tomic.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Sir, I'd like to start and spend some minutes -- take us some time to go through a bit of what we might call background to try to clarify a few points that we discussed last week, perhaps a few more points on particular items or clarification. I'd like to start off, please, in terms of the HDZ political party. You said last Monday that you were pressed or pressured, in 1991, to become a member of the HDZ, but that you did not become a member "at that time." Could you tell us, please, who was pressing you to join the HDZ in approximately 1991?

utterances.speaker: NEVEN TOMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: At the time, the municipal leadership of the HDZ of Mostar offered me to sign their papers and become an HDZ member. That would have made it easier for me to become appointed a director of the reconstruction and development fund of the city of Mostar. To answer your question, it was the municipal leadership of the HDZ of Mostar.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Two things, sir, that you're going to find that I will ask you repeatedly, and if you can assist not only me but the Judges, please. When you say "municipal leadership," I'm even more interested in getting the names of actual individuals, if you can assist us, and I'll also be asking, I'll just say in general about dates. If you can be as specific as possible, everyone being mindful, of course, that these events took place some time ago, but if you can assist us as much as possible with dates, that would be appreciated. So when you say someone in the municipal leadership or people in the municipal leadership wanted you to join the HDZ, picking up on what I just said, such as who, what individuals?

utterances.speaker: NEVEN TOMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mr. Jerko Doko, Milivoj Gagro, Marin Topic.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: And I take it from the implication of the answer that you gave when you said you did not join "at that time," that you did at some point join the HDZ; correct?

utterances.speaker: NEVEN TOMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Later, as the HVO of the HZ-HB and political bodies continued working, all members of the HDZ were invited to the Presidency sessions, and later on we became members of the HDZ, firstly by our functions or positions, and then in practical terms we became members of the HDZ.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: All right. So you've answered my question. You did at some point become a member of the HDZ. Can you tell us, again, dates? Approximately when was that?

utterances.speaker: NEVEN TOMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I've just told you that there's no specific date. We did not sign any papers to become members. It was just a string of events. Continued activity had ensued, and all officials in the HZ-HB and later on in the government of the Federation were duty-bound to attend Presidency sessions, and they were also members of the main board of the HDZ. Not for a single moment there was anything as the official signing of any papers, so I wouldn't really be able to give you any precise date.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Well, sir, I don't want to get too bogged down in this, but let me just suggest to you I don't find that answer to be sufficient. It certainly was not the case that just anyone and everyone sort of at some point morphed into an HDZ member in the general population or among the officials of these various bodies, so, sir, you must have some idea when you considered you had become a member of the HDZ. Please.

utterances.speaker: NEVEN TOMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: If I can compare the periods in question, I can tell you that I became a party member after I went to Sarajevo; in other words, after the Washington Accords, in that period roughly.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Let's come at it this way: When you became involved with the Mostar Crisis Staff in 1992, by approximately April/May 1992, did you consider that you had become a member of the HDZ by that time?

utterances.speaker: NEVEN TOMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: And you can't assist the Judges any more as to when you became a member of the HDZ, except at some time between 1991 and going to Sarajevo sometime after the Washington Agreement years later, sometime in there you became a member of the HDZ; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Objection. Mischaracterizes the evidence. He said after he went to Sarajevo, which would have been after the Washington Agreement, so we're talking post-1994, post-indictment period. That should be helpful to the Judges.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: That's what I said, Mr. Karnavas. It says "and going to Sarajevo sometime after the Washington Agreement, years later."

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Are you saying, sir, you were not a member of the HDZ until after the Washington Agreement, which was signed in approximately March 1994?

utterances.speaker: NEVEN TOMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: There was no official admission into the membership of the HDZ. I did not sign any papers to join. At that moment, the HDZ was a movement rather than anything else, and as per the HDZ rules, we were all duty-bound to participate in its work. I really can't give you the precise date when I consider to have become a member of the HDZ, because there was no official admission act that preceded it.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: And did you hold any other positions or functions in that party, apart from membership? Did you ever become an official or take on any sort of other function or positions in the HDZ party during the time that you were a member?

utterances.speaker: NEVEN TOMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: By function, as the deputy presiding over the Ministerial Council, I was also a member of the Presidency of Bosnia-Herzegovina. This was through sheer --

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: I apologise. Our time is limited, and I ask you to listen to my questions very carefully. If it's mis-translation or if I misspoke, I apologise both to you and to the interpreters. My question had nothing to do with the Ministerial Council or your position in the Presidency of the Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina. Sir, right now I'm talking about the HDZ political party. You understand the concept of a political party, I take it. Yes?

utterances.speaker: NEVEN TOMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, of course.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: You understand my question to you now is: Did you hold any offices, position or function in the HDZ political party, other than being a member?

utterances.speaker: NEVEN TOMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was a member of the Presidency of the HDZ of Bosnia-Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: When did you become a member of that body?

utterances.speaker: NEVEN TOMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In early 1997, when I was elected the co-chairperson of the Ministerial Council.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Prior to being a member of the HDZ, were you a member of any political party in your adult life?

utterances.speaker: NEVEN TOMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was a member of the League of Communists.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: You said in your testimony last week that for approximately one year, you were the president of a Yugoslavian youth organisation of some sort. Unless I missed it, and I may have, can you give us the name of that particular organisation that you were the president of?

utterances.speaker: NEVEN TOMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was the Alliance of the Socialist Youth of Yugoslavia, and I was the president of the municipal conference of that organisation, i.e., of the Alliance of the Socialist Youth, in the municipality of Mostar.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: What time period -- for what time period, sorry, did you hold that position, approximately?

utterances.speaker: NEVEN TOMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: For a year, precisely.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues]... what date, precisely?

utterances.speaker: NEVEN TOMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe that it was in 1985 and in 1986.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Is there any relationship -- and this may seem very basic to you and it may be known to most everyone in the courtroom or not, but for purposes of the record in this case, can you tell us what relationship, if any, existed between that organisation and the Communist Party or League of Communists?

utterances.speaker: NEVEN TOMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This organisation rallied young people, up to the age of 27. It was a collective member of the Socialist Alliance of the Working People of Yugoslavia, which was a collective organisation which comprised the League of Communists as the leading force in that organisation.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Now, apart from being president of the Socialist Youth, did you have any other -- hold any other positions or office in that party, in the Communist Party?

utterances.speaker: NEVEN TOMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was a member of my own organisation, in the Unis Electronic Company in Mostar.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Apart from that, did you hold any party positions? Were you a secretary, a president, a chairperson? Did you hold any other functions in the Communist Party, other than those you've told us about so far?

utterances.speaker: NEVEN TOMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: None, as far as I can remember. I did not hold any important functions.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Prior to the time you became head of the finance department of the HVO in approximately mid-August 1992, prior to that time, had you held any government function in the former Yugoslavia at any level, municipal, regional, federal, republic? Had you held any political office or governmental office, excuse me, prior to becoming head of the finance department?

utterances.speaker: NEVEN TOMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was, in professional terms, the director of the fund for the reconstruction and development of the city, and during that period of time I was not politically active, in terms of being affiliated with any political party during that period of time.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: All right. Did you consider this fund to be, then, based on your answer just now, a governmental body, a public body, as opposed to a private business, or perhaps socially owned, mixed in some way? But if you can just briefly clarify, please.

utterances.speaker: NEVEN TOMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The reconstruction and development fund was a para-budgetary institution which managed public resources. In other words, it managed funds, financial funds that belonged to the Municipality of Mostar, and those funds were intended for the zoning, urban planning, development, and reconstruction of the infrastructure. It also managed the assets in terms of building ground and infrastructural facilities.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: When you say -- when you describe that as being a para-budgetary organisation, what do you mean in that context, "para" meaning what?

utterances.speaker: NEVEN TOMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The fund had its own budget which was passed at the annual level and which was ratified by the Municipal Assembly. However, it was not part of the municipal budget, and it is within this context that I said that it was a para-budgetary institution. It did have a budget but not as part of the municipal budget. However, the city assembly had to approve its budget, and thus it had a say in defining the projects and plans that this fund passed at its own level.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: And then you were appointed head of the HVO finance department on the 15th of August, 1992; correct? Maybe the 14th, but middle of August.

utterances.speaker: NEVEN TOMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: And then later in the fall of 1993, perhaps around November, after the Croatian Republic of Herceg-Bosna was established, you were named deputy finance minister under Mr. Martinovic, as finance minister; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: NEVEN TOMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: And you were appointed once again to the top finance position, if you will, as Minister of Finance of the Croatian Republic of Herceg-Bosna in January 1995; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: NEVEN TOMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: And you held that position for approximately how long, sir, until when? If you can give me kind of an end date, please.

utterances.speaker: NEVEN TOMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe that it was up to the moment when the governments of the Federation and the Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina were split. This was the moment when the Washington Agreement took off the ground, which happened just before the Dayton Accords were passed.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: So sometime in late 1995, then; is that what you're telling us?

utterances.speaker: NEVEN TOMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I would say mid-1995, but I can't be sure of the exact time when this happened.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: So you held -- just to be sure here, you held the position of Minister of Finance of the Croatian Republic of Herceg-Bosna only from approximately 13 January 1995 to mid-1995; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: NEVEN TOMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I really can't tell you exactly when my office reached the end, because during that period I was also the Minister of Finance of the Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina, the Federation of Bosnia-Herzegovina and Herceg-Bosna, when the governments of the Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina and the Federation of Bosnia-Herzegovina split, at that moment my office in the government of Herceg-Bosna was terminated.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: During the period of approximately 1 April 1992 until the end of 1992, can you tell us where you lived or had your residence, your principal residence, please?

utterances.speaker: NEVEN TOMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In Mostar.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: And approximately -- can you give us the address in Mostar, please?

utterances.speaker: NEVEN TOMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: First in my own apartment in Leopold Dokmanovic Street, number 3, and later in Mr. Slezak's house, which was not far from my own apartment.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: And did you continue to live at -- the second location, then, if I understand correctly, if it's a matter of sequence, did you continue to live at that residence in 1993?

utterances.speaker: NEVEN TOMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: In an effort to try to save some time, if we can - maybe we will, maybe we won't - I'd like the witness to be shown or provided a copy of -- we will provide the witness a copy of what was previously marked as P09517, which is a street diagram of Mostar Town; not in great detail, but it's one we've used on a number of occasions.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: If the Chamber wants to look at it, it will be on the ELMO. It should also be in e-court, the clean version, as, I believe, again, P09517.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Sir, I'm going to ask you to make some markings. So if the usher can assist you with the appropriate marking device. Sir, if you can find it on the map, approximately, and again I realise and everyone realises this is not a detailed map, but if you can give us the approximate -- as best you can, the approximate location of the first place that you told us that you lived a few moments ago in Mostar before you moved into Mr. Slezak's flat, I believe. Where was that, if you can make a mark, you can mark that with a number 1, find it and then mark it number 1.

utterances.speaker: NEVEN TOMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks].

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: And then where was the second place of Mr. Slezak's residence?

utterances.speaker: NEVEN TOMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The place isn't on the map.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Can you kind of point an arrow and just maybe make -- give it a number 2 and just point it off in the general -- as close as you can to the general direction off the map, where it was?

utterances.speaker: NEVEN TOMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks].

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: All right. And my question to you at the time we pulled out the map was: And did you continue to live at location number 2 throughout 1993 or where did you live in 1993?

utterances.speaker: NEVEN TOMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: On the whole, I lived there.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: All right. And during the time when you were working at the -- once you became involved as the head of the HVO finance department, so we're talking about August 1992 and forward, can you tell us where your office was located? When you went to work, if you will, as head of the finance department, where did you go during that second half of 1992? Mark that number 3, please.

utterances.speaker: NEVEN TOMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks].

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Thank you. And for how long did you work at that particular location, approximately?

utterances.speaker: NEVEN TOMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was until the left bank was finally liberated and when we moved to Hotel Arrow.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: And when was that, approximately? That is, when did you have your office at Hotel Arrow?

utterances.speaker: NEVEN TOMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think it was at the beginning of 1993.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Can you mark that, please, with number 4?

utterances.speaker: NEVEN TOMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks].

utterances.speaker: JUDGE TRECHSEL
utterances.text: Excuse me, Mr. Karnavas [sic]. Mr. Tomic, you have used the expression that the left bank was liberated. Liberated from whom? What do you have in mind when you use that term?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, when it was liberated from the presence of the Yugoslav Army and reserve forces present in the area.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Maybe -- I'm sorry, Judge.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE TRECHSEL
utterances.text: I leave it at that for the moment.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Perhaps Judge Trechsel would have the same follow-up question.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: That leaves me just a bit confused, because I thought you said that in August 1992, you were working at location number 3. August 1992 would be after the Serbs left Mostar, so I think your dates are a bit confused, if you'll allow, sir.

utterances.speaker: NEVEN TOMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, correct, but Hotel Arrow was destroyed. It had to be renovated, and when we accumulated the initial equipment, when this was started on, so I think it was the beginning of 1993 that we moved to the premises of Hotel Arrow. I can't be precise, though.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE TRECHSEL
utterances.text: A very brief technical question. Mr. Tomic, how would you spell the name "Arrow," the name of the hotel? How do you write it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] E-R-O.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE TRECHSEL
utterances.text: Thank you. That's what I thought, but it's "Arrow" in the transcript, which is something -- I don't know, perhaps this is a translation, but thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: All right, sir. So then just based on the clarification the last few minutes, from approximately August 1992 until approximately sometime in early 1993, your office was located at number 3. Sometime beginning in early 1993, you relocated your office, that is, the finance department, to location number 4. How long were you at that location number 4?

utterances.speaker: NEVEN TOMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: We were there until the conflict between the Muslims and the Croats in Mostar broke out.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: So until approximately May 1993, the 9th of May; is that what you're telling us?

utterances.speaker: NEVEN TOMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: And where did you move your location? I do understand that at some point you indicated you had moved the location to Siroki Brijeg. Was it at that time?

utterances.speaker: NEVEN TOMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: And how long did you remain in Siroki Brijeg for? Did you at some point return to Mostar, and if so, when?

utterances.speaker: NEVEN TOMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, we remained in Siroki Brijeg for about a month, perhaps, and then we returned to Mostar, to the new premises, which is where the finance department continued with its work.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: So when you moved to a new location in approximately June 1993, can you please find that on the drawing and mark that number 5.

utterances.speaker: NEVEN TOMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks].

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: And did you remain at that location through the rest of 1993 and into 1994, "that location" being number 5?

utterances.speaker: NEVEN TOMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, and then later on I think we moved to the Praktent [phoen] building. I had left for Sarajevo already, so I don't know when that was exactly.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Well, let me -- again, sir, so that the record is clear for the future, did you remain at location number 5 through at least maybe -- and we don't know exactly when yet, but through at least the end of 1993?

utterances.speaker: NEVEN TOMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think so.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Now, when the office relocated for about one month to Siroki Brijeg, did you continue living in Mostar or did you also move your residence to Siroki Brijeg?

utterances.speaker: NEVEN TOMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: My flat remained in Mostar.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: And if it's -- can you tell us, then, where you were living during that period of time? It may be one of the -- presumably, it's one of the markings you've already made, so where were you living? Were you living at location number 2 throughout this period?

utterances.speaker: NEVEN TOMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: And if I can ask you a similar question to what I asked you a moment ago: Did you continue to live at that location until at least the end of 1993?

utterances.speaker: NEVEN TOMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think so.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Now, where was -- you've told us where the finance department was located. Where did the HVO HZ-HB have its office ? And again we'll start chronologically. When you became finance head in mid-August 1992, where was the HVO HZ-HB located? And can you -- when you've found that on the map, if you can mark that number 6, please.

utterances.speaker: NEVEN TOMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, at the time when Mr. Prlic was designated as the president of the HVO HZ-HB, he set up an office which was in the same building in which the finance department was located, so it's number 3 here.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Just so we can keep the record very, very clear, could you mark a number 6 just very close to the number 3?

utterances.speaker: NEVEN TOMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks].

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: But not "36." Why don't you draw a line, if you could, please, between the "3" and the "6." You can just draw a diagonal line between the "3" and the "6." My apologies if I've confused it.

utterances.speaker: NEVEN TOMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks].

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Now, did it remain at that location, sir, through all of 1992 and 1993, or did the HVO HZ-HB move its office at some -- excuse me, at some time?

utterances.speaker: NEVEN TOMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: After my department moved to Hotel Ero, immediately afterwards the HVO also moved the office of the president of the HVO and other departments; justice, the department for refugees, et cetera.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: If I can still remember, forgive me, is it number 4, location number 4?

utterances.speaker: NEVEN TOMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: And could, in the same fashion, sir, could you draw maybe a diagonal line to separate the "4" and then mark that with the number 7?

utterances.speaker: NEVEN TOMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks].

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: So is it correct, sir, that during the time when the finance department was located at locations 3 and 6 and again at locations 4 and 7, you were at the same locations with Mr. Prlic and the HVO HZ-HB?

utterances.speaker: NEVEN TOMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct. At number 3 and 6, we were there all the time together, and 4 and 7 -- at 4 and 7, Mr. Prlic's office arrived a little later, but then there was a period of time during which we were both there.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: And did Mr. Prlic's office remain at the location 4 and 7 throughout the remainder of 1993 or did it -- did his office or the HVO HZ-HB, or what became the HR-HB government, did that location change at some point?

utterances.speaker: NEVEN TOMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it changed.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: And can you look on the map, please, and when you think you've found the approximate location, can you mark that with a number 8?

utterances.speaker: NEVEN TOMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks].

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: And can you tell us approximately how long did Mr. Prlic and the HVO government or the HR-HB government, whichever it was at the time, how long were those operations located at location 8?

utterances.speaker: NEVEN TOMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think it was until our departure to Sarajevo. I think the HVO HZ-HB was there until that point in time.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: So again using sort of the measure that we used earlier this afternoon, at least until the end of 1993; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: NEVEN TOMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: All right, sir, we're almost finished with this, but a few other locations I'd like to ask you about. We're going to talk in a few minutes about your history and relationship with Mr. Prlic, but I take it that during the years 1992-1993, you knew where Mr. Prlic lived. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: NEVEN TOMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: And again if we start with approximately April 1992, during the time of the Special-Purposes Council, for example, and the Crisis Staff, where do you know -- where was Mr. Prlic living around that time? And when you find that location, approximately, can you mark that as number 9?

utterances.speaker: NEVEN TOMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks].

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: And again, using my -- it could have started sometime well before that, but starting at least by, let's say, May 1992, how long did Mr. Prlic continue to live at location number 9, or did he live at that location until at least the end of 1993?

utterances.speaker: NEVEN TOMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mr. Prlic at that point in time was living with me and two of my friends at location number 1.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: When you say "at that time," when was that? You've just told us a moment ago that his residence was at location number 9, at least as at April/May 1992, in that time period. When did he move to location number 1?

utterances.speaker: NEVEN TOMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: During that period of time, he moved, because his family had also moved to Makarska. The flat was located in an area that was vulnerable to shelling from Hum. He then moved to my flat, which had a better location given the shelling or shooting from the Hum hill and Podvelezje.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: All right. Now -- and I'm sorry if I misspoke about location number 1. Is that the time after you had moved in with Mr. Slezak or -- let me rephrase my question. When Mr. Prlic moved in with you, was that at location number 1 or location number 2?

utterances.speaker: NEVEN TOMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Location number 1.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: And how long did Mr. Prlic live with you at location -- at that location number 1?

utterances.speaker: NEVEN TOMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: We moved to location number 2 together.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: And again remind us, at this part of the record, when was that?

utterances.speaker: NEVEN TOMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think it was at the end of 1992.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: And how long did Mr. Prlic live with you at that location? And if it helps or if it helps move us along: Did the two of you continue to live at that location until -- at least until the end of 1993 together?

utterances.speaker: NEVEN TOMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: And, again, to be very, very clear, we're now talking about location number 2; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: NEVEN TOMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: And I think only one other location that I want to ask you about. Where was the HVO Department of Defence located? And again we're starting April 1992 and moving forward. Where was the HVO Department of Defence, the place where Mr. Stojic had his office?

utterances.speaker: NEVEN TOMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, first of all in Grude, and then an office was established in Mostar.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Let's go to the time -- excuse me for interrupting you, but in the interests of time, let's go to the point where the office was located in Mostar, since that's the map that we're looking at at the moment. When was a Department of Defence office located, in the sense that we're using it now, Mr. Stojic's office of the Department of Defence, when was that located in Mostar? And if you can find it on the map, sir, I think we're up to number 10, please.

utterances.speaker: NEVEN TOMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks].

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: And how long did Mr. Stojic and the Department of Defence have its main office at that location, number 10?

utterances.speaker: NEVEN TOMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't say precisely. I know that they later moved to another building, but I don't know exactly when.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Another building in Mostar, in West Mostar?

utterances.speaker: NEVEN TOMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Mr. President, if we could have an IC number for the map, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, this document shall be given Exhibit number IC 00877. Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Moving to --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Witness, one follow-up question. We've learned that you were sharing a flat with Mr. Prlic. Did you pay rent or did -- we would like to know who paid the rent.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I paid the rent, and he and two of my other friends were in my flat because it was safer there, and it was easier for us to obtain logistics, to do logistics matters, because my wife and children weren't there. When I say "logistics," I mean kitchen work and so on.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] My last question: To your knowledge, did Mr. Boban have a service flat, or did he stay with someone, or did he live in his own house without this apartment being paid for either by the Republic of Herceg-Bosna or the Croat Community?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] As far as I know, Mr. Boban had a house in a village in the suburbs of Grude. It was a privately-owned house.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: And just to stay on that moment -- for a moment longer, then: Did Mr. Boban at any time, to your knowledge, in 1993 have either an office or a residence in the town of Mostar?

utterances.speaker: NEVEN TOMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: There was an office for the president of the HZ-HB which moved to location 3 or, rather, 6 on this map, when the HVO HZ-HB moved to Hotel Ero.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: I suppose that leads us, then, to the next question. You've told us there was a physical office. How often was Mr. Boban, in your experience, how often was Mr. Boban himself actually in Mostar during this time? And, I mean, we're roughly talking mid-1992 until the end of 1993, about an 18-month period. I mean, you may have had an office, but perhaps you will tell us he was never there or perhaps he was there every day.

utterances.speaker: NEVEN TOMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: He would come very seldom. He spent most of his time in Grude.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Now, we're still on locations, but changing gears a bit. During this time period we've been talking about this afternoon so far, roughly, again, April 1992, end of 1993, did you have occasion to be in Sarajevo?

utterances.speaker: NEVEN TOMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Did you have any regular points of contact there, and by that I mean did you have friends, business associations -- associates, excuse me, political colleagues? Did you have any persons in Sarajevo during that time period you had regular contact with?

utterances.speaker: NEVEN TOMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't have regular contact because there were no communications in that situation, and on the whole, when they left Sarajevo, well, on such occasions it was possible for me to meet some of them.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Well, just to make it a bit more specific, if we can, just let me ask you about a couple of particular individuals. There may have been times during that time period, again mid-1992, end of 1993, when, maybe or maybe not, Mr. Franjo Boras may have been in Sarajevo. Did you have any regular dealings during this period with Mr. Boras at any time that he was in Sarajevo?

utterances.speaker: NEVEN TOMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I didn't.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: How about Mile Akmadzic, did you have any dealings or communications with Mr. Akmadzic during the time when he was -- if any, when he was in Sarajevo during that time period?

utterances.speaker: NEVEN TOMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: When he came to Herzegovina is the first time that I met him. I had no contact with him while he was in Sarajevo.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: And just a couple of additional names. How about Mr. Bozo Rajic? Did you have any dealings with Mr. Rajic in Sarajevo during this time period, mid-1992, end of 1993?

utterances.speaker: NEVEN TOMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Bozo Rajic was the vice-president of the HZ-HB, and as far as I know during that period of time, he wasn't in Sarajevo, he was in Grude, Citluk, and I know that his family was in the same hotel where my parents were. So I would see him over the weekend, too, at the Adriatic.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: And I take it that was in Makarska. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: NEVEN TOMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Basko Polje, which is near Makarska.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Sir, can you tell us when you first met Jadranko Prlic?

utterances.speaker: NEVEN TOMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: We knew each other from the streets, from town, but we actually met each other when I was the president of the youth organisation, and that is when we started cooperating more seriously, because at the time he was also the secretary of the Socialist Association of the Working People of Mostar, another political organisation.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Is there any short or more common or familiar name for that particular organisation, other than Socialist Association of the Working People of Mostar? I mean, is it the Communist Party, sir, just so we're clear?

utterances.speaker: NEVEN TOMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. It's an organisation which included all political organisations or covered all political organisations active in the town of Mostar at the time of Yugoslavia. It included the Communist Association, Communist League, the youth organisation, and the Association of Combatants, trade unions. All these bodies were members of this, well, let's say umbrella organisation.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: All right, I understand.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Tomic, this organisation which brought together a number of organisations, was it typical to Mostar or was this the Communist system at that time that structured things in that way everywhere?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That was the structure, starting with the federal level, where there was the so-called Socialist Alliance of Working People of Yugoslavia. Then there was such an organisation in every republic and also in every municipal, across the board.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well, thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: And did you understand, sir, and again so that we don't get bogged down in some of these -- some of the terminology too much because of time limitations, during that time period did you understand Mr. Prlic to be a member of the Communist Party?

utterances.speaker: NEVEN TOMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: And would it be fair to say, sir, that from that time forward, it may have, if I can use the term, ebbed and flowed a bit, but from that time forward until recently, maybe even today, you and Mr. Prlic have been good friends; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: NEVEN TOMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Later on, I cooperated with Mr. Prlic in the government of the city of Mostar, which was known as the Executive Board, of which he was the president and I was the director of the finance or revenue administration. Our relationship during that period of time was mostly official. We did not socialise privately.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Let me interrupt you there for a moment, sir, with my apology. During what period of time, again dates, what period of time was Mr. Prlic the president of the Executive Board and you were the director of the finance or revenue administration? Can you give us dates for that, as best you can, a start date and an end date?

utterances.speaker: NEVEN TOMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That was after 1986. The term of office was for one year, the time, so I wouldn't be able to give you the exact year, but for one year he was the president of the city government.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: If we use 1986 as the time when you were involved in this socialist youth organisation, and then we know that you and Mr. Prlic took on certain positions in August 1992, so we're talking about a span of some six years, can you give us some better idea of when, during that time period, Mr. Prlic was the president of the Mostar Executive Board or Council?

utterances.speaker: NEVEN TOMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't remember the year. I know that he was in office for one year, and then for two years it was Gojko Krsman, but I can't give you the exact years. That was the time when I stopped being with the youth organisation, until 1990. He went to Sarajevo after that and became vice-president of the government there. I can't give you any more precise indication of the year.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] You were the mayor of Mostar in the year 2000, you told us last week. We have just discovered that Mr. Prlic was the president of the Executive Board for the town of Mostar in 1986, seemingly, or after 1986. So before you, he had headed the Municipality of Mostar; is that right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, at the time he was the president of the city government for one year.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In other words, you held similar positions, both of you, but you in the year 2000 and he more than ten years prior to your time?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Similar, but the system changed and the office of mayor was introduced. The system would be similar, but still different.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This is what I had understood.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Sir, going back to my original question, with this additional explanation and some additional questions which I put to you, which I thank you for your answers, the original question that I put to you was: From that time forward, though, and we went back to the time that you were both involved in the socialist youth and related socialist organisations that you've already discussed with us, from that time forward you and Mr. Prlic have been business or political/governmental associations and also good friends; correct?

utterances.speaker: NEVEN TOMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: We were not good friends at that time. We did not socialise outside the --

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: My apologies to the witness and interpretation, but again time is precious. When did you become good friends with Mr. Prlic, because you did become -- you are good friends with Mr. Prlic, sir, so approximately when, and have you continued to be good friends with him?

utterances.speaker: NEVEN TOMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct. That was after 1992, when he returned from America. That's when I saw him, when he came to Mostar. And since his family had already left Mostar, he then moved together with two other friends and started living in my apartment, and I --

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Excuse me. And is it fair to say, then, from at least 1992 and would you consider to the present time, that is, till today, that you are close friends with Mr. Prlic, notwithstanding the current circumstances?

utterances.speaker: NEVEN TOMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Now, you said that when you took over the office of finance department head in August 1992, that you found no documents, you found -- could not find what we might call any work product by Mr. Prlic, there didn't seem to be an office, there really didn't seem to be much of anything, and lest the Chamber draw perhaps the wrong conclusion from that, let me try to clarify that with you. Do you mean to communicate to the Judges by that that Mr. Prlic was in effective or not doing anything at the time, or was it the case, sir, in fact, that the HVO HZ-HB and its departments were not really operational or doing much until Mr. Prlic became president of the HVO HZ-HB in mid-August 1992?

utterances.speaker: NEVEN TOMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Up to then, the finance department was not really established, it did not have a premises, it did not have manpower.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: And just so the record is clear, Mr. President, and I know that it will be corrected, but just so there's no confusion, in the answer at page 25, line 22, the answer was: "Correct ," the answer to the previous question: "Correct," and starting with the word "Now," of course that starts the next question. I just noticed that.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: All right. Well, my question to you is focusing more on Mr. Prlic than the premises or the operation of the office. Would you say, in your experience, that Mr. Prlic is a very -- in fact, a very competent, in fact, very talented administrator?

utterances.speaker: NEVEN TOMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Would it be fair to say that Mr. Prlic is the type of person who we might say, and forgive me, I don't know if you have it in your language, but we might say the type of person who dots his "i"s and crosses his "t"s?

utterances.speaker: NEVEN TOMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's what he always tries to do, to dot his "i"s and cross his "t"s.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: In addition to his considerable capabilities, would it be fair to say -- would it be fair for the Judges to understand that Mr. Prlic, throughout this time period, was also a very ambitious man?

utterances.speaker: NEVEN TOMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: What period do you have in mind?

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: 1992, through the 1990s, in fact even before that. You indicated he was the president of the Executive Council, then he was the vice-president of the Bosnian government in the 1980s, early 1990s, then he went to Sarajevo on business, then he came back, he became the president of the HVO. He took on subsequent senior positions as a pretty young man; correct?

utterances.speaker: NEVEN TOMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Would it be fair for the Judges to understand that Mr. Prlic, in addition to being very capable, was a very ambitious man?

utterances.speaker: NEVEN TOMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Witness, in your eyes is the term "ambitious" a quality or not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This is good -- a good thing in a person and a wish to achieve success in one's job.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: And if we can just again try to work on the dates a bit. I see something here that perhaps may assist us, if you agree or not. In finding a date when Mr. Prlic was, in fact, the deputy prime minister of Bosnia and Herzegovina, if I suggested to you, based on some documentation, that that was from approximately 1989 to 1991, does that sound correct to you?

utterances.speaker: NEVEN TOMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: In addition to being very capable, ambitious, did you also find, in your dealings with Mr. Prlic, both as a friend, as a business colleague, as a political colleague, that he was rather adaptable to the circumstances around him?

utterances.speaker: NEVEN TOMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mr. Prlic, as an educated person, could adapt to the circumstances that prevailed, and he could easily react to all of them.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Well, let me put it to you this way, sir: Would it be fair to say that when it was good to be a communist, Mr. Prlic was a good communist; when it was a good to be a Croat nationalist, an HVO president, he was that; and when it was later good to become a moderate, then he held himself out as a moderate?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Objection to the form of the question. These are facts that have not been established. Now, if he wants to go one by one, he perhaps can ask an open-ended question, such as, "Was Mr. Prlic ever a nationalist?" So the question presumes facts which are not in evidence, and I object to the form of the question.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Your Honour, I think the question exactly asked the witness to give the answer. It is -- it's not a "yes" or "no" question, necessarily. It's for him to say -- I asked him a question about being adaptable, and the witness said: "Yes. In fact, as an educated person, Mr. Prlic could adapt to the circumstances that prevailed." To simply illustrate my point, I asked the next question. I believe the witness can answer the question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Scott, I believe that your question is very complex. It's a question that could have been broken down into several questions, because he can answer in the negative. You can put the question to him again, if you like, and we'll see what he says.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. Let's perhaps come back to it with some additional -- after some addition evidence has been covered.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: The two of you during this time period, 1992, 1993, 1994, had occasion to travel together when he was president of the HVO and you were the head of the finance department?

utterances.speaker: NEVEN TOMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: And just as one example that I came across, the two of you travelled to Zagreb together in March 1994 and, I believe, shared a room at the Intercontinental Hotel in Zagreb during times when you were meeting there with President Tudjman or the Croatian government; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: NEVEN TOMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, but we did not share one room. We each had our own room.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Well, perhaps you can turn to Exhibit P08138, and if we can pull out the binders for perhaps the first time. P08138, binder number 2.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] One moment, there's a question. Judge Mindua.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MINDUA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Scott, I have a short question. I'm a little bit uncomfortable with the question you put to the witness. You wanted to know whether the accused Prlic was an ambitious man. Would this not be speculation, insofar as we have no objective facts to substantiate this? For instance, whether this man was an educated man, that can be substantiated with facts. But you did not pursue the matter.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Your Honour, we have a witness before us who's known Mr. Prlic since the late -- since the 1980s, probably something at least something like 30 years in a variety of contexts, and I believe this witness in fact is an excellent person to give us his assessment and comment on Mr. Prlic and the person he is. So I'll leave the testimony for the Chamber's consideration, of course.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Sir, if you can find -- and I don't mean to spend a lot of time on it, but just since you mentioned it, if you can find Exhibit 8138. And do you recall Mr. Susak's secretary, Ms. Zlojic [phoen], who I think either at that time or later became the wife of Mr. Gotovina, who is also on trial in this institution, do you recall Ms. Zlojic, Mr. Susak's secretary, making -- booking for one room for you and Mr. Prlic at the Intercontinental Hotel in March 1994? That's one double room in your hotel for 31 March and 1 April 1994 under the names of, 1, Mr. Jadranko Prlic; number 2, Mr. Tomic. Does that refresh your memory?

utterances.speaker: NEVEN TOMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know that we were at the Intercontinental Hotel and that we had a double room each.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: All right. Well, be that as it may, was that normally the way -- when you would travel to Zagreb on business to meet with various government officials there, such as Mr. Tudjman, Mr. Susak and others, would the Croatian government arrange your hotel room and travel for you?

utterances.speaker: NEVEN TOMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Sometimes we would bear our own cost, and during this particular period of time the Ministry of Defence had a location and a price agreement with the Hotel Intercontinental, so that we would only approach that ministry to reserve our rooms through them.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: All right. Mr. President, I see the time and I'm about to change topics. If that might be a time for a break.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We shall have a 20-minute break.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Scott, you have the floor. [No interpretation].

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Mr. Tomic, if we can go back for a moment to the locations in Mostar, and I think we can do it without having the map. That will save a bit of time, perhaps. Location number 2, you had indicated, was what we might call the north edge -- the top -- or the top side of the map or the north edge. Well, let me not confuse the issue by saying "north." At the top of the map as oriented as we were looking at it. And you said the location was off the map. Just so it's clear, can you tell us, what was the street address? If you can't show it on the map, can you give us the approximate street address of the location that was off the map?

utterances.speaker: NEVEN TOMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was a small street which intersected with the street of Blajburg victims. The street was so small that it only had four house numbers, approximately.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: And when you say "off the map," can you give us some idea, again for the future, are we talking about a hundred metres off the map, are we talking about a kilometre; how far off that map in that direction of your arrow was that location?

utterances.speaker: NEVEN TOMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Looking at intersection denoted by number 2, it would be some 200 to 300 metres away from that intersection.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: And finally, sir, on that point: During the time when you and, I understand, Mr. Prlic were living at location number 2, and given the various locations -- your office locations also marked on the map, how did you travel from the place that you were residing to the office locations where you worked?

utterances.speaker: NEVEN TOMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I had a vehicle. I had a driver as well. He would drive me to the place where my office was.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: And was that true, to your knowledge, for Mr. Prlic as well?

utterances.speaker: NEVEN TOMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, he also had a driver.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Now, going back to some of the positions that Mr. Prlic held at various times, just before we move forward, after he was -- after he left as the president or head of the Herceg-Bosna government, did he at some point become the Minister of Defence in the Federation?

utterances.speaker: NEVEN TOMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Approximately when was that and how long, approximately, from date to date did he hold the position of Defence minister?

utterances.speaker: NEVEN TOMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe that this was during the period from our arrival in Sarajevo, which was in mid-1994, after the Washington Agreement and the moment when the Federation government split from the government of the Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: And as to that second event, you still can't recall approximately when that was, or can you?

utterances.speaker: NEVEN TOMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe that this was in mid-1994, if my memory serves me well. I apologise. It was in mid-1995.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: All right. Sir, in terms of this case, apart from Mr. Karnavas, have you talked or met with anyone about your testimony in this case or what you expected, before coming here, what you expected your testimony would be?

utterances.speaker: NEVEN TOMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I spoke to Mr. Karnavas and his team.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: And have you met or spoken to any of the accused since this trial began in April 2006?

utterances.speaker: NEVEN TOMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: During their stay in Croatia, when they were provisionally released, I met Mr. Pusic; only him, of the six of them.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: All right. Have you spoken to or met with Mr. Prlic during that time period, since April 2006 to the present day?

utterances.speaker: NEVEN TOMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: And when was that, please?

utterances.speaker: NEVEN TOMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: When he stayed, i.e., when he was provisionally released, I took an opportunity and visited him on one occasion just for one day.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: When, approximately, was that, sir, the best you can; month, year?

utterances.speaker: NEVEN TOMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Every time when he went out, we would meet for a day.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: And you would meet for a day. So you would spend a day together whenever Mr. Prlic would be provisionally released?

utterances.speaker: NEVEN TOMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Those were mostly family visits around lunchtime or just for cakes and tea in the afternoon, so it would not take a whole day. At the most, it would be a couple of hours.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: All right. So let me make sure I understand, sir. Would it be fair to say, then, and if I'm wrong, then I'm sure you'll say so, but would it be accurate to say that on each occasion when Mr. Prlic has been on provisional release in this case, whenever that has been, that you've always spent some time with him during that time?

utterances.speaker: NEVEN TOMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: When you have met with anyone in connection or on behalf of Mr. Prlic, in connection with this case, has anyone, while talking to you, taken any notes or operated any sort of recording device?

utterances.speaker: NEVEN TOMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't have the opportunity of speaking to a lot of people about this case. I did speak to someone --

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Let me assist you. Now I'm talking about the group of people working with Mr. Karnavas. And I'm not asking you to tell us at this moment anything -- let me be very clear. I'm not asking you to tell us anything about what Mr. Karnavas or his associates may have said or not said to you. But during any times when you were being questioned, meetings with you, interviewed, was anyone taking notes or operating any sort of recording device?

utterances.speaker: NEVEN TOMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: They mostly took notes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: And have you ever signed anything that might be described as a statement or any sort of record of what you've said during a time that you were meeting with anyone acting on behalf of Mr. Prlic? Did anyone later give you a recording or give you a statement and ask you to review it in any way and affirm it, in any way? Whether you signed it or not, you said, "Yeah, that's what I said"?

utterances.speaker: NEVEN TOMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I didn't sign anything.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: You indicated to Mr. Karnavas that in recent days, you had -- or sometime -- strike that. I'm not sure exactly when, but at some point you provided him with approximately 54 documents. What were the -- what was the source of those documents?

utterances.speaker: NEVEN TOMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: These were documents from my own private archives.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: How large a private archive would you say you have? Do you have hundreds of documents, or just these 54, or how many documents from this time period, 1992, 1993, 1994, how many documents do you have?

utterances.speaker: NEVEN TOMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have the documents that I submitted. These documents were ones that had to do with the Council for Special Purposes, which did not have an archives of its own. Those documents, or some of them, remained with me, at I was one of the coordinators within that council, and there was some documents that have to do to the period that was subsequent to the Washington Agreement and had to do with the negotiations between the Croatian and Bosniak side with regard to establishing a financial system. These documents were in my possession. I, in fact, don't have any other private documents.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Excuse me, sorry. I think we got the rest of your answer. My apology. Apart from the -- strike that. When you say that you had these documents from back during the time, are these all documents that you had kept -- just you had kept them personally throughout this time period or were any of these documents provided to you by someone else?

utterances.speaker: NEVEN TOMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: These documents were ones that I had myself, on the whole, and no one gave them to me.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Did you meet with a man named Cvikl in December 2007?

utterances.speaker: NEVEN TOMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Where did you meet him?

utterances.speaker: NEVEN TOMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In Zagreb.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Who arranged that meeting?

utterances.speaker: NEVEN TOMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was through Mr. Karnavas' office.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: And how long would you say that you spent with Mr. Cvikl on this occasion in December 2007?

utterances.speaker: NEVEN TOMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Three or four hours.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: And during the time you were meeting with Mr. Cvikl, was anyone else in the room or involved in these matters, or was it just the two of you, you and Mr. Cvikl?

utterances.speaker: NEVEN TOMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Just the two of us.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: And where did you actually meet, physically? I know Zagreb, but a hotel, an office, your home -- or, sorry, strike that, not your home, but where?

utterances.speaker: NEVEN TOMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Hotel Intercontinental, which is now called Hotel Westin.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: And during that time period, sir, I'll ask you a question similar to the one I asked you a few minutes ago. Was Mr. Cvikl taking notes, or operating any sort of recording device, or making a record of his conversation with you during that three- to four-hour period, did you say?

utterances.speaker: NEVEN TOMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: He noted a few things on a piece of paper.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: And did you understand at the time, sir, when this was arranged, that Mr. Cvikl was apparently talking to you in connection with preparing a report that would be given to the Judges in this case?

utterances.speaker: NEVEN TOMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's what he told me.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Did you provide any documents to Mr. Cvikl?

utterances.speaker: NEVEN TOMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Since you began giving your testimony at approximately 9.00 last Monday morning, have you spoken with anyone about your testimony? And I mean anyone.

utterances.speaker: NEVEN TOMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Apart from my wife, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Apart from the documents that have been shown to you in the courtroom, have you seen or looked at any materials or documents or notes of any sort related to the subjects of your testimony since beginning your testimony, other than what you've been shown in the courtroom?

utterances.speaker: NEVEN TOMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In the proofing session, I saw a certain number of documents.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: All right. And my particular question to you now, sir, is that: After your testimony began last Monday, have you seen -- apart from the documents that Mr. Karnavas or now myself or anyone else has shown you in the courtroom, have you looked at any other -- consulted any other materials or information outside the courtroom?

utterances.speaker: NEVEN TOMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Going back to the time period that we've been talking about primarily today, that is, approximately mid-1992 until April -- excuse me, the end of 1993, excuse me, did you ever have any conversations or direct meetings or involvement with Mr. Izetbegovic?

utterances.speaker: NEVEN TOMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mr. Izetbegovic visited Mostar towards the end of 1992, I think, and on that occasion I met him.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Did you ever, apart from meeting him -- well, was that meeting in -- are you considering that to be pretty much of a social occasion, in terms of you were somewhere together, you introduced yourself and met him, or were you participating in an actual, you know, meeting of some sort together?

utterances.speaker: NEVEN TOMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: He spent two days in Mostar, I believe, and on one day we had a meeting in the headquarters of the HVO HZ-HB. It was chaired by Mr. Prlic. Mr. Izetbegovic and his delegation attended that meeting on that day or on the following day. It was Bajram Muslim holiday, so we also socialised on a private basis. This, I think, was organised by the Muslim organisation called Preporod or Rebirth.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: And apart from that occasion then, sir, did you have any communications or dealings with Mr. Izetbegovic during this period mid-1992 to the end of 1993?

utterances.speaker: NEVEN TOMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: And I take it, sir, what I suspect the answer will be, but again just so the record is very clear: Did you attend any meetings or sessions of the Presidency of Bosnia-Herzegovina during the period mid-1992 to the end of 1993?

utterances.speaker: NEVEN TOMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Did you attend any meetings of the government of Bosnia-Herzegovina, if we might use the term "Cabinet," not the Presidency, but the group of people around the prime minister? Did you have any occasion to attend any meeting or session of that group during the period mid-1992 to the end of 1993?

utterances.speaker: NEVEN TOMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't attend any sessions. I had contact with individual members who would come to Mostar, and on one occasion there was a meeting in the headquarters of the office of the government in Zagreb.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: You attended that meeting, I take it, the one in the office of the government, as you describe it, in Zagreb.

utterances.speaker: NEVEN TOMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, on one occasion I was there.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Approximately when was that?

utterances.speaker: NEVEN TOMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think it was towards the end of 1992.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: And just so there's -- again so there's no confusion in the future, when you say "the office of the government in Zagreb," I took it -- I understood you to be saying this was some sort of office operated by the government of Bosnia and Herzegovina in Zagreb, not the Croatian government. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: NEVEN TOMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct. It was the office of -- the office of the government of Bosnia and Herzegovina in Zagreb.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: In connection with your work with the HVO HZ-HB, was there something in the HVO method of working or process called a work programme?

utterances.speaker: NEVEN TOMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: There was no such programme in the form of a document at the beginning or initially; only later on.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: And later on, approximately when?

utterances.speaker: NEVEN TOMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think it was in 1993 or 1994.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: And who would prepare these programmes? Sorry, my apologies. Let's go back for a step -- let's go back a step. What was the purpose of these programmes?

utterances.speaker: NEVEN TOMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, the departments had to present their activities for the upcoming period and state what their financial needs were in order to operate.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: And so each department would prepare these programmes from time to time?

utterances.speaker: NEVEN TOMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: So, for example, in the finance department, you would prepare, or someone working on your behalf, which perhaps you would ultimately approval and sign, you or your staff would prepare a programme -- a work programme for the finance department; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: NEVEN TOMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: We prepared such a programme within the department. I signed it and then sent it to the HVO HZ-HB, which would then adopt a consolidated programme, which we would then discuss. And on the basis of this programme, we could then see what the activities of other departments for a given period were.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: And was this done on an annual basis, a quarterly basis; how often would these programmes be prepared and submitted by each department to the HVO HZ-HB?

utterances.speaker: NEVEN TOMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Initially, very seldom, every three months, but I believe that the first real programme was drawn up for 1994, and it included a budget as an integral part of that programme.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: All right. Now, going back -- going back for a moment, before we turn to some other topics, to your history with Mr. Prlic. Have you and Mr. Prlic ever been involved in business together or any business ventures, investors in the same projects? Have you conducted business or been investors together during the time of your friendship?

utterances.speaker: NEVEN TOMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, we were never co-investors in the business sense.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: So, for example, are you saying, sir, that the two of you have never been involved in business together or invested together, for example, in businesses dealing with oil?

utterances.speaker: NEVEN TOMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Never.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Did you ever have anything to do with a company called Interina Mostar?

utterances.speaker: NEVEN TOMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's a branch firm of Ina in Zagreb, which provided Bosnia and Herzegovina with oil.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: And did either you and/or Mr. Prlic have any dealings, investments, involvement in that company?

utterances.speaker: NEVEN TOMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: You said a few moments ago that you met with Mr. Prlic, if I understand correctly, on each occasion -- or have met with him on each occasion when he's been on provisional release. Do you recall approximately the last time you met with Mr. -- or spent time with Mr. Prlic while released?

utterances.speaker: NEVEN TOMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This summer in Makarska.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: The summer of 2008, to be accurate?

utterances.speaker: NEVEN TOMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: And you mentioned on one occasion, if I'd heard correctly, that you'd also met Mr. Pusic. Approximately what date was that?

utterances.speaker: NEVEN TOMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I met Mr. Pusic this summer, too.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: And where?

utterances.speaker: NEVEN TOMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In the Westin Hotel in Zagreb.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: All right. And maybe I heard correctly or maybe I didn't. Is that the only time you've met Mr. Pusic or have you met him on other occasions?

utterances.speaker: NEVEN TOMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: We also met when he was there on one previous occasion.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Where?

utterances.speaker: NEVEN TOMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In a cafe in Zagreb.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: And approximately when was that?

utterances.speaker: NEVEN TOMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I couldn't say precisely. I know that I was there with my two children. I just came to greet him because I was going on a trip. But as to when that was exactly, I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Concerning the Mostar Crisis Staff, although Mr. Karnavas did indeed ask you the question several times, I'm not sure that we ever really got a full answer. You were a member of the Mostar Crisis Staff in May 1992; correct?

utterances.speaker: NEVEN TOMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I was an associated member.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: What does it mean to be an associated member?

utterances.speaker: NEVEN TOMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, it means that the Crisis Staff designated me and my colleague, Kazazic, to deal with certain activities in the sphere of finance.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Sir, during that time, on behalf of the HVO, what was the HVO or the HDZ, whichever of these organisations you want to refer to at that time, you were the principal organiser of finances during that time period; correct? I mean, you weren't just an associated member. You were the finance man, weren't you?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Excuse me, Your Honour. I think the question is rather unclear. Are we still during the period of the Crisis Staff, when he was appointed by Gagro and others?

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: During that -- sorry, excuse me, Mr. Karnavas. Yes, that's correct, Mr. President, that's the time I was referring to, in reference to the Crisis Staff.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: You were the principal person dealing with finances during that time, weren't you?

utterances.speaker: NEVEN TOMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. The principal person was a member of the Crisis Staff, Mrs. Bulka [phoen]. She was the secretary for Finance for the Mostar municipality before the Crisis Staff was established, and she became a member of the Crisis Staff. I and my colleague Kazazic were subsequently appointed, because the financial sphere wasn't functioning properly. We were engaged for special operations that had to do with the public accounting service at the time. I wasn't the main person dealing with finance. I had been appointed by the Crisis Staff to deal with certain matters.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: So that we have it correctly in the record, it may be that it's -- it may be that it is, but "Bulka," can you spell Ms. Buljko's last name, please?

utterances.speaker: NEVEN TOMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: B-U-L-J-K-O. Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Thank you very much. All right. Well, I'm just wondering, then. Did she continue to be the principal finance person, then, throughout the summer and fall of 1992 or did you take on that position or responsibility at some point during that time period?

utterances.speaker: NEVEN TOMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In August, I was appointed as the head of the finance department of the HVO HZ-HB. From the time when the Crisis Staff fell apart, well, at that time I was a member of the Council for Special Purposes, whose task it was to protect property, to administer property and companies, in the sense of establishing the preconditions for defence and for supplying the population and staff members of companies. This body didn't have an administrative character, in the sense of administering of public finances.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: All right. Let's go forward, then, to the time when you became the head of the finance department. Let me just take us through some things and see if we can -- if we can avoid going to all the documents, we will try to do that. The HVO HZ-HB was set up and functioned with a number of departments in the government, is that correct; Defence, Finance, Interior? There were a number of departments that were -- that reported to the HVO HZ-HB; correct?

utterances.speaker: NEVEN TOMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: And, in fact, the HVO HZ-HB consisted of or was comprised of the president, vice-presidents, the department heads and potentially other members; correct?

utterances.speaker: NEVEN TOMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.
