utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: So during the second half of 1992, that included, among others, Mr. Prlic, as president, Mr. Stojic, as head of the defence department, and yourself as head of the finance department; correct?

utterances.speaker: NEVEN TOMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: And the head of each department was responsible for the work of that department; correct?

utterances.speaker: NEVEN TOMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: And you reported -- as the head of each department, you reported and were accountable to the HVO HZ-HB; is that right?

utterances.speaker: NEVEN TOMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: We submitted reports, programmes and reports on the work -- on our work to the HVO HZ-HB and to the Presidency of the HZ-HB.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Just a minor intervention, Your Honour, for future purposes. The previous question was compound, and of course it's very difficult to say "yes" or "no". You know, reported, accounted, now, those are two different aspects, so I would kindly ask that we go, you know, one fact per declarative statement with the inflection, thus making it a leading question, as opposed to making it compound. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: I'll try to do better, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Sir, would you agree that -- and I'm referring to some of the HVO documentation at the time, if anyone wants to look at it. I'm referring to P00303, 3 July 1992, amended statutory decision on the organisation of the executive body. But you would agree, wouldn't you, that it was the HVO HZ-HB which was to regulate the work of each department; correct? Correct?

utterances.speaker: NEVEN TOMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: There are decisions that determine what the work of each department is.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Sir, the HVO regulated the activities, structure, operational framework and powers of the departments; correct?

utterances.speaker: NEVEN TOMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Departments had authority on the basis of decisions on establishing these departments.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: The HVO supervised the work of the departments, and the HVO had the ability to annul or abolish anything that a department did; correct?

utterances.speaker: NEVEN TOMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The department tabled proposals, and they were autonomous in their proposal submission. The HVO discussed the proposals, and as a result the texts were corrected and amended, and finally if the head of the department was in agreement with the corrections, the proposal that was tabled was voted on, and that's how our regulations were passed in the HVO HZ-HB.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: All right. Well, let's go to Exhibit P00303, then. It should be in the first binder, sir, and it will be tabbed hopefully for you in numerical order. And I believe, sir, if it will assist you or orient you, I don't know if they are organised in a similar fashion in Mr. Karnavas' documents or not, but you'll find the English translation on top and then you'll find the Croatian language version behind it. If you could find 303. And once you've done that, could you please turn to Article number 6 or find Article number 6. Article 6 provides, does it not: "The HVO shall regulate the activities, structure, operational framework and powers of its departments in accordance with regulations passed by the Presidency"; correct?

utterances.speaker: NEVEN TOMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: And turning to Article 14: "The HVO shall supervise the work of its departments and municipal HVOs. The HVO may use its supervisory power to annul or abolish individual legal acts passed by the bodies referred to in the foregoing paragraph." Do you recall any occasion in which the HVO annulled or abolished any act taken by the finance department during the time when you were head of the finance department? Not "didn't approve" in the sense of initial proposals were put on the table, there was a vote, they were voted up or down, but once something -- you had done something, you had taken some action, you had taken a step on something, you had made a departmental decision, do you recall any occasion when the HVO annulled or abolished or, if you will, undid that action?

utterances.speaker: NEVEN TOMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I can remember, there was just once when a municipal decision was discussed. I can't remember which municipality it was. And that's the only thing that I can remember within that particular context.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Tomic. Let me go back and clarify my question, although you certainly anticipated another question, in any event. Focusing for a moment on the Department of Finance, the department that you were the head of, do you recall any acts or decisions of your department that were abolished or undone by the HVO HZ-HB?

utterances.speaker: NEVEN TOMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I can't remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: You can't remember that there ever was one or you can't remember one way or the other?

utterances.speaker: NEVEN TOMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't remember a decision which was annulled. I should say the HVO, of its own will, annulled a decision. If a department proposed something, it was a correction or a change of a decision which the HVO then adopted. But for the HVO to raise an issue on its own initiative and to annul a decision, I can't remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, with a bit of reservation, because I don't know whether this is due to interpretation or recording error, my learned friend read paragraph 14.2, where it says: [In English] "Annul or abolish individual legal act," individual -- [Interpretation] "Individual" is the operative word here which has to be stressed. According to our traditional administrative doctrine, there are the so-called general administrative acts like a decision decree, something that applies to a wide range of subjects, and there are also individual administrative acts or documents which apply to a very specific legal person, i.e., to the existence or non-existence of the rights of a certain person. Paragraph 2 regulates individual administrative documents or documents that apply to individuals. That's what my learned friend has just warned me to something that is the literal wording in the text. So the situation is entirely different here. We cannot apply this to HZ-HB deciding on a decree that they themselves passed or its department or municipality. That is according to paragraph 1. However, we are now discussing paragraph 2.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Kovacic, you are currently testifying.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I just wanted to explain in order to put a correct and fair question to the witness. My learned friend Scott is not a Croatian lawyer and he does not know the system, and the witness himself cannot understand the system because he is not a lawyer. I just wanted to explain things. I believe that in your states, given the tradition, there is a system division when it comes to administrative documents. That's as far as I can remember from my school days. I just wanted to remind you of these things. However, the fact that my learned friend is putting questions to the witness about paragraph 2, i.e., the individual documents and at the same time he is talking about general documents pertaining to paragraph 2, this is confusing. This is not the way to do things.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Scott.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Sir, if you'll look at Article 13, you'll agree that it provides: "The HVO has the right and duty to annul a regulation passed by a department or other administrative body which is detrimental to the general interest or which contravenes established policy or positive law." Do you see that and, secondly, did you understand that to be, in fact, the power of the HVO?

utterances.speaker: NEVEN TOMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, this defines certain powers. For example, if I, as a department head, issue an instruction contrary to the instructions passed by the HZ-HB, in keeping with this article the HZ-HB is allowed to annul such a regulation. However, I don't remember any such thing ever having happened in my practice. I can't remember that.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: If you look, please, next at Article number 9, the same document, it provides, does it not: "The HVO president shall be in charge of the work of the HVO," that is, Mr. Prlic, "and shall be held accountable for it. He shall ensure the unity of the political and administrative activities of the HVO, cooperate with other bodies and organisations of the HZ-HB, and direct the activities of the HVO as a whole and its members as individuals." So when you filed these reports and, among other things that you talked about a few moments ago, these departmental documents that would be prepared, for example, they would ultimately go to, among others, to Mr. Prlic as president; correct?

utterances.speaker: NEVEN TOMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, they are addressed to the office of the president and, as such, they were delivered to his office.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: In Article 7, the second clause, it says: "The Presidency of the HZ-HB," and I think everyone in the courtroom knows that's referring to the legislative body: "The Presidency of the HZ-HB shall appoint and dismiss the other members," and this is a section talking about the composition of the HVO, "at the proposal of the HVO president." So would you agree, sir, that Mr. Prlic had the ability, he had the power, to propose the appointment and dismissal of other members of the HVO HZ-HB?

utterances.speaker: NEVEN TOMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, this is as per Article 7.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: And just as an example, to your -- during the time that you were a member of the HVO HZ-HB, did Mr. Prlic ever propose the dismissal of Mr. Stojic as head of the Department of Defence?

utterances.speaker: NEVEN TOMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know anything about that.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: You don't know anything or, to your knowledge, that never happened? Mr. Prlic, to your knowledge, never proposed the dismissal of Mr. Stojic as head of the defence department; correct?

utterances.speaker: NEVEN TOMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know about that.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: During the time from August 1992 to August 1993, did Mr. Prlic propose the dismissal of any department head?

utterances.speaker: NEVEN TOMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know that the secretary of the HVO was replaced.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: When was that?

utterances.speaker: NEVEN TOMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In late 1992, I believe, the gentleman who did not perform properly or according to expectations.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Who was that, sir, by name, please?

utterances.speaker: NEVEN TOMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mr. Ivan Tomic.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Any relation?

utterances.speaker: NEVEN TOMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: And your understanding is that Mr. Ivan Tomic is removed from his position as secretary of the HVO because of, essentially, incompetence or ineffectiveness?

utterances.speaker: NEVEN TOMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, there were objections by several departments, and a particular problem was the fact that he did not organise the publication of the Official Gazette. As a result of those objections, he was dismissed from that position.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: So the HVO HZ-HB did have the power and at least on one occasion did have the ability to remove and dismiss people from positions; correct?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Your Honour, can we be a little more specific? "People," you know, we're talking about a secretary versus a department head, so perhaps --

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Anyone.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Anyone, sir. We went over the last few minutes that the department heads report to the HVO, that they file reports, that they're accountable to the HVO, and we indicated that the Presidency, in Article 7, the second clause, you may recall, sir, provided that the Presidency of the HZ-HB shall appoint and dismiss the other members of the HVO government at the proposal of the president. Now, other members of the HVO government are, among others, the department heads; correct?

utterances.speaker: NEVEN TOMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was talking about a procedure to dismiss the secretary. The HVO had appointed the secretary, and as a result of objections by departments, he was dismissed. I don't know of any situation in which heads of departments or members of the HVO were treated in the same way, because the secretary of the HVO was not a member of the HVO. He was just an administrative officer on behalf of the HVO.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Well, let's go back to Article 7 of P00303. Article 7 provides: "The HVO shall be comprised of: The president, vice-presidents, department heads and other members." Who was included in "and other members"?

utterances.speaker: NEVEN TOMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Heads of sub-departments, because there were also sub-departments as a category. For example, the sub-department for education, culture and sports. It was a sub-department. However, its head was a member of the HVO.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: All right. Well, building on all that, sir, and perhaps as some clarification I come back to a similar question to one I asked you a few minutes ago: To your knowledge, sir, during the period from August 1992 until the end of 1993, did the HVO president, Mr. Prlic, propose, as provided in Article 7, the dismissal of any member of the HVO HZ-HB, including any of the department heads?

utterances.speaker: NEVEN TOMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know that this happened.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Let's go to document P09530, which will be the last document in binder number 2. P09530. These are the rules of procedure of the HVO HZ-HB that were put in place, apparently, in November -- at least by November 1992, according to the first page. In fact, I believe they were actually signed by Mr. Prlic on the last page on the 14th of October, 1992. Sir, if I can direct your attention, please, to Article 8, and the document is such that there is -- there's another decision on the front of it, Your Honour, just the way the documents were compiled. But when you get down to page 3, you will get to the rules of procedure of the Croatian Defence Council of the Croatian Community of Herceg-Bosna. And in that document, sir, if you can go to Article number 8. I asked you earlier about the programmes of work, and this is a section actually going up to Article 7 in the section, it's called "Programming of Work," and it says: "The programme of work shall be adopted by the HVO. The president and the secretary of the HVO shall supervise the implementation of the programme of the HVO." Article number 9: "The bodies of the HVO shall be bound to implement the programme of work and monitor its execution. In case of their failure to execute the tasks set by the programme of work, the bodies of the HVO shall be bound to submit a timely report on the reasons for the failure to the president of the HVO." Now, these programmes -- these programmes were, in fact, being submitted as early as the end of 1992 and early 1993, weren't they?

utterances.speaker: NEVEN TOMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: When it comes to finance, we drafted monthly or quarterly budget proposals, and in the second half of the year 1993, was the realistic time for the preparation of these programmes. The book of rules was issued towards the end of October 1992, and it clearly defines everything. In other words, we submitted the programme of work for our respective departments, as their heads, and we submitted those to the HVO, who then issued a consolidated/coordinated programme of work and monitored its execution. And if my department was not in a position to secure the finances in time, I was duty-bound to inform the HVO about that. This served for the other departments that were tied with the Department of Finance to be able to adjust the rate of their activities. In other words, no money, no reconstruction of a facility building, and that then had to be moved forward to another period, and so on and so forth.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Is it correct, sir, that the other departments, just like the finance department, to the best of your knowledge, proceeded on the same basis; they prepared programmes, work programmes, and which were submitted to the HVO, and made reports to the HVO, and indeed were accountable to the HVO; correct?

utterances.speaker: NEVEN TOMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Excuse me. In Exhibit 9530, if we go to Article 47, which is quite a bit further down into the document, please -- excuse me, my apologies. I've sent you to the wrong place, but it's close. Not so close. Article 13. My apologies to everyone. If you go back to Article 13, sir, page 6 of the English version, actually then carrying over to the top of page 7, the second item on page 7 says: "The opinion of the Department of Finance relative to the necessary funds, sources, and the manner in which the enforcement of the regulations and other enactments will be funded." Now, this was an opinion, as I understand it, that was required in connection with any sort of proposed decision or policy coming before the HVO HZ-HB. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: NEVEN TOMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: For each document, for each rule that involved cost or revenues, an opinion had to be obtained from the Ministry of Finance or Department of Finance.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Could we characterize that as something like a financial impact statement, that it was -- if a particular decision or action was proposed, it was up to the Department of Finance to determine how that decision or action or programme would affect the financial capacity of the HVO?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE TRECHSEL
utterances.text: Excuse me, Mr. Scott. I'm slightly lost. Could you indicate again where, exactly, you are quoting from?

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, I'm sorry. My apologies.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Page 5.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Page -- I'm at the top of page 7 of page 9530, in Article 13, and the language I was referring to a few moments ago was the opinion that would be rendered by the Department of Finance.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE TRECHSEL
utterances.text: I must rule in favour of Mr. Karnavas. I find this is page 5 in the document I have before me.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: All right. Maybe we've got --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE TRECHSEL
utterances.text: "L 0024396" on the top.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: We must have different page numbers. I apologise for that. If we're looking at Article -- can we find -- can we agree that we're looking at Article 13?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE TRECHSEL
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Well, I don't know what happened. I must have a different translation. My apologies. My Article 13 is on page 6 and 7, and my apologies to the courtroom for that.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: But under Article 13, there is a beginning paragraph which says: "The documents shall be submitted." Then there are three what might be called bullet items under that, the opinion of the Commission for Regulations, the opinion of the Department of Finance, the opinion of the Department of Justice and Administration, and I'm focusing on the opinion of the Department of Finance, and I apologise for the confusion. So going back to my question, sir, is this something that essentially your department was responsible for, some decision or action would be proposed, and you had to assess the financial impact on the HVO, where the funds would come from, how this would be carried out financially; is that correct? Is that what this is about?

utterances.speaker: NEVEN TOMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is regulated by Article 13.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Yes. And what I just put to you, sir, is that a proper description of what this is really about? Some action or policy would be proposed, and it was up to your department to do some sort of financial analysis as to the financial impacts of such decision or action on the HVO, where the funding would come from, et cetera? Is that what this is talking about?

utterances.speaker: NEVEN TOMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This was a customary procedure for passing regulations, and that's how it was incorporated in the document. However, in practice, the letter of the document was not followed through fully.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: All right. Well, we'll eventually come to some additional documents on that. Now, if you could go in the Defence binder -- binder of Defence exhibits, which is the fourth binder -- it's a smaller binder, and I don't know if it's labelled binder number 4, but the fourth binder, which is 1D 02136. Sir, this is a document that I believe we looked at earlier, if I'm not mistaken, last week. Just related to what we were just talking about, was it also part of the responsibility of your department to make financial projections, if you will, as to the revenues or funds that would be collected and available to the HVO government for conducting its operations, and is that reflected on 1D 02136?

utterances.speaker: NEVEN TOMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, in accordance with the decree on the budget for the HZ-HB, the finance department had to secure the funds for the functioning of the department, and in accordance with that decree the departments needed to submit their requests on a monthly basis and every three months. We're still discussing a period during which there wasn't an entire budget for the HZ-HB. We had monthly plans and quarterly plans. Here we have a conclusion from a period when there were additional obstructions in municipalities for paying revenue into the budget, after the conflict broke out between the Muslims and the Croats, and on that occasion I reported to the HVO HZ-HB and informed them that funds weren't being found. And this conclusion, in fact, confirmed our duty. It's all in the law on the budget. But given the situation, this just emphasised the fact again.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: It's correct, is it not, and you testified about this last week, that the various department heads would bring their financial needs to the HVO HZ-HB, including Mr. Stojic on behalf of the Department of Defence, and among other things, each department head would brief, if you will, inform the HVO HZ-HB about the work of its department -- of his or her department and situations they were involved in; correct?

utterances.speaker: NEVEN TOMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: And in terms of financing, this particular document 1D 02136 relates to defence financing, would it be fair to say that that includes -- I'm talking about financing defence, that includes such things as logistics?

utterances.speaker: NEVEN TOMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, financial sources run out and for defence needs, well, it was necessary to assess the revenue coming in for the following month.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: But apart from revenue, when you look at such things as logistics, that would include such things as -- well, in the military context, that would include such things as manpower, wouldn't it, personnel? You can't have an army without soldiers, can you?

utterances.speaker: NEVEN TOMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, funds were allocated to the defence department. Funds were allocated up until the budget was established. And as I said, the first budget, which clearly specified what would be allocated to staff for material needs, for special purposes, well, the first budget was for 1994, the first such budget. During this period, funds were allocated to the defence department, and they used these funds in accordance with their programme and needs.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Sir, you testified last Wednesday that the usual thing -- the usual way how things are done is that through financing and logistics, there is civilian control over the army. Civilian control over an army is established and exercised largely through its control over financing and logistics; correct?

utterances.speaker: NEVEN TOMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: We financed the defence department, so it comprised a number of sectors, all of which represented the way in which that department functioned.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: And that was one of the ways -- some of the important ways, sir, is it not correct, that the HVO HZ-HB exercised power and control over the departments, including the Department of Defence, was through such things as financing and logistics; correct?

utterances.speaker: NEVEN TOMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Through the working programme and the report on work. These were the means that the HVO HZ-HB could use to influence certain departments, and that included the Department of Defence.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Well, let me just come back to your statement last week, sir. Do you still agree today, as you said last week, that two of the ways that a civilian government controls the military is by its control of such things as financing and logistics? You agree, don't you? Sir?

utterances.speaker: NEVEN TOMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I apologise. Just a minute. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Could you look, please, next at Exhibit P09063. That will be in binder number 2, P09063. Sir, just coming to this topic, and I'm trying to, in the interests of time, not go through all the documents that we could, because we'd never have time, unfortunately, to do that, but I did have a couple of questions to you about this document, if you have P09063. Looking over your shoulder, sir, I don't think you have it yet. P09063 in binder number 2. Sorry for the confusion. It's a copy of Mr. Prlic's business card which another witness had provided to us in this case that she had obtained back during the time of 1992-1993. Just a couple of questions about that card. Of course, Mr. Prlic is described -- or gives the title of president of the HVO HZ-HB. There's two telephone numbers listed. Did you ever use those two telephone numbers to call Mr. Prlic or communicate with Mr. Prlic during 1993?

utterances.speaker: NEVEN TOMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: And there's also a fax number there, did you ever -- do you recall whether you or your staff, if you will, ever communicated with Mr. Prlic's office during 1993 by fax?

utterances.speaker: NEVEN TOMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't think so.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: And there's also a listed mobile telephone number, 099-470-508. With that in mind, can I ask you, first of all, did you have a mobile phone back at the time 1992-1993?

utterances.speaker: NEVEN TOMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: At some point in time in 1993, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: And were you able to use that to communicate with people in Bosnia-Herzegovina?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Excuse me, could we be a little more specific? Bosnia-Herzegovina is a pretty large place, and it's divided at this time, so are we talking about areas in the Republika Srpska, Sarajevo?

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Everywhere. My question was intentionally broad.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Could you call -- you can correct me or limit your answer however you wish. Could you communicate with people throughout Bosnia and Herzegovina by your mobile phone during that time period?

utterances.speaker: NEVEN TOMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: We could use mobile phones only to phone outside of Mostar, because in Mostar there was no signal for mobile phones to use.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: And what was the coverage area outside of Mostar, sir?

utterances.speaker: NEVEN TOMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, mostly it included the territory of Herzegovina, and from Herzegovina it was possible to phone Croatia, Slovenia, Europe.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: And to your knowledge, do you recall using this number for Mr. Prlic from time -- the mobile number 099-470-508, did you have occasion to call Mr. Prlic on that mobile number from time to time?

utterances.speaker: NEVEN TOMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Could you please go to Exhibit P00824, which will be in the first binder. P00824.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE TRECHSEL
utterances.text: May I just add a little question to the previous one.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Of course.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE TRECHSEL
utterances.text: Mr. Tomic, could you also call Sarajevo with a mobile phone?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE TRECHSEL
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Scott, that was all.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Thank you. Thank you, Judge Trechsel. Sir --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Just a minute. Mr. Praljak.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED PRALJAK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour Judge Antonetti, I believe there is something that isn't quite precise here. The witness said: "We could only call outside of Mostar." I believe one should clarify whether they could phone from Mostar or whether they had to go outside of Mostar to do that, because outside of Mostar means --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I think the answer was very clear. The witness told us that he could not call Sarajevo. However, Witness, with your cellphone, could you call abroad? I guess you could, and you could call from Mostar and surrounding; is that what you said?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE TRECHSEL
utterances.text: Sorry, I had understood Mr. Praljak's question in a different way. Mr. Praljak wanted to know whether it was possible to call from Mostar, and I think the witness has clearly said in Mostar you couldn't use it, you had to go outside. That's -- it's clear, okay.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That's correct. In Mostar, well, the technology was quite new at the time. You could capture the signal in Herzegovina, and Mostar is in a valley, so we had to leave Mostar in order to phone. In Bosnia and Herzegovina, in Sarajevo, this technology hadn't been set up yet. The communications network had been destroyed and it was not possible to use this new technology to phone Sarajevo, because at a given point in time the signal has to go down to the ground and then use regular telephone lines, which at the time had been destroyed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It's clear, then, rather than calling Mr. Prlic, that would have forced you to leave Mostar, and he would have had to be out of Mostar, too. It was easier just to go see him, visit him, or use the regular phone line?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, in Mostar, after part of the capacity had been repaired, after some of the equipment had been repaired, it was possible to phone from office to office. But in order to use mobile phones, we had to, for example, both be outside of Mostar so that we could communicate with each other, because there was no signal for those mobile phones in Mostar.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It's clear. Thank you. It's time for the break also, Mr. Scott. Twenty minutes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The court is back in session.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Mr. Tomic, before the break we were looking -- or we were just beginning to look at, I believe, P00824, and just a couple of points. And I'll tell you now -- I'll forecast what I'm going to ask you, and that is: If this is just -- this and another document or two that we're going to look at gives us an idea of the type of business that came before the HVO HZ-HB on a regular basis. For example, in this set of minutes from the 27th of November, 1992, and if I can ask you to turn to item number 9, and the English version is the top of the third page and I hope it's the same translation, but it's item number 9 in any event, for example, it says: "Draft decision on the refugees and expelled and displaced persons office is submitted by the HVO HZ-HB Secretariat. The decision was adopted unanimously." Item 10: "The head of the HVO HZ-HB finance department, N. Tomic, nominates Drago Bagaric, a qualified economist from Begonja, for director of the HVO HZ-HB customs administration, and Miljenko Karacici is appointed the acting director of the HZ-HB Official Gazette. The stated proposals were unanimously adopted." Now, is that -- are those fair examples of the kind of business that came before the HVO HZ-HB on a regular basis; approval of decisions or programmes, personnel appointments, that sort of thing?

utterances.speaker: NEVEN TOMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Item 9 states that the HVO took a decision on establishing an office for refugees. It was under the Presidency of the HVO HZ-HB, which didn't really hold a session. Item 10 has to do with appointing lower-ranking individuals in the department, as suggested by the head of the department. Appointments were to be made by the HVO HZ-HB at its session, and that was done. In the case of the customs administration and in the case of the Gazette.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: If you go toward the end of the document, and in the English version it will be the top of page 5, you can see the end of the document, sir, and go up approximately three paragraphs, just one other example I'd like to show you to -- to show to you because it relates to the finance department. It says: "At the proposal of the head of the HVO HZ-HB finance department, N. Tomic, a unanimous decision was adopted on the manner of allotment of financial aid to the municipal HVOs in Central Bosnia." Again my question to you: Is that representative of the sort of the financial business that would come before the HVO HZ-HB on a regular basis?

utterances.speaker: NEVEN TOMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Up until the time that a budget was adopted for the HZ-HB, funds were allocated on the basis of decisions that were prepared by departments, at the request of individual departments or users, and it was done in accordance with funds available. Decisions on the matter would then be taken by the HVO HZ-HB. If there was a budget, an organised budget, it would have been done automatically as the budget was adopted. But since such document was not in existence, individual decisions had to be taken.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Could you go, please, to 1D -- it's in the fourth smaller binder in the Defence exhibits, 1D 01669. 1D 01669. And while you're looking for that, sir, this is a set of minutes from the HVO HZ-HB meeting on the 5th of July, 1993, as always listing those in attendance, including, for example, Mr. Prlic, Mr. Zubak, Mr. Stojic, Mr. Tomic, Mr. Buntic, Mr. Perkovic, Mr. Palameta, et cetera, and again some particular items I just want you to take a quick look at. Item number 6 on the bottom of page 2 of the English version, but in any event, sir, if you can find item number 6: "The draft decree to establish a commission for the exchange of prisoners and other persons was submitted by the Secretariat. Following a decision involving the participation of Mr. Maric, Mr. Saric and B. Pusic, the following was concluded:" And then we see action taken following that, including the appointment of Berislav Pusic as head of the service. So you would agree with me, sir, this is another example of the HVO HZ-HB carrying out its personnel powers in the appointment of Mr. Pusic to the head of this body; correct?

utterances.speaker: NEVEN TOMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is a decision that was taken because the Presidency of the HZ-HB wasn't functioning. The initial commission was appointed by Mr. Boban before, so this decision was taken in order to establish its structure because it was only formed by individual members, and in this decision its authority was specified and Mr. Pusic was appointed as the head of that body.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: As another example, going further down to item number 7, item 1, item 7, number 1, it says: "Mr. Z. Buntic shall once again request from Mr. A. Markotic a report on the demographic situation in the HZ-HB." Could you explain to the Judges, please, what the interest of the HVO HZ-HB was in the demographics in Herceg-Bosna?

utterances.speaker: NEVEN TOMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I can remember, I think it had to do with the implementation of the Vance-Owen Plan.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: And do you recall, in fact, receiving a report after -- sometime the 5th of July from Mr. Markotic on the demographic situation in Herceg-Bosna?

utterances.speaker: NEVEN TOMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't remember. I know that he worked on maps and that he was a professor of demographics.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Well, my -- very well, but my question to you -- so, sorry, you don't remember one way or the other?

utterances.speaker: NEVEN TOMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I don't.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Excuse me. Looking at item number 8, it says: "Mr. B. Stojic told the session about the military and security situation in the territory of the HZ-HB. Following the Muslims' latest attacks, the response to the mobilisation was rather good." And was that, again, generally the way things happened at these HVO meetings, that among other department heads, Mr. Stojic would give a report on the military and security situation?

utterances.speaker: NEVEN TOMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: From time to time, we were informed of the problems the defence department had, and also of the situation in the field that we had to be aware of because of the activities of the individual departments, because the activities in the field were directly related to re-establishing communications, re-establishing the public auditing service. These were things that other departments had to be aware of when carrying out their tasks.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: If we could go next to item number 12, the last item. It says: "All bodies and services of the HVO HZ-HB shall submit reports on their work, with a short assessment of the current situation in their sphere of activity for the period between 1 January 1993 and 30 June 1993; deadline, 12th July 1993." And is that again representative of the type of process that was followed by which various reports would be filed from time to time with the HVO HZ-HB?

utterances.speaker: NEVEN TOMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This was a biennial report. There was also an annual report when all the departments submitted reports on what had been done and also provided assessments with regards to the activities in their domain, with regard to whether certain tasks had been accomplished or not, and also with regard the future tasks that had to be dealt with.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: And there's some other points in that document that I would like to cover if we had more time, but I think that's all the time we can spend on that particular item. If I could ask you, please, to go next to P01652, which will be in the first binder. P01652. Again, sir, this is a set of minutes from the HVO meeting on the 11th of March, 1993. It's indicated that you and others were present, Mr. Prlic, Mr. Stojic and others. I'm going to ask you to go to -- it's on the -- the pages have been organised rather strangely on this in some ways on the English translation, anyways. But if you can find point 13, I think it will assist us. There are a number of points in the document, point 1, point 2, and if you get toward the end of the document, you'll see point 15. If you go up to point 13, I'm not really interested in point 13 but what's right above it. Right above point 13, sir, it says: "At the proposal of the Office for Refugees, Expelled and Displaced Persons of the HVO HZ-HB, Nevenko Herceg is appointed office secretary. The proposal on the appointment of the HVO of Kresevo municipality is adopted. The proposal is enclosed." Now, again these were both personnel decisions, if you will, being approved by the HVO HZ-HB; correct?

utterances.speaker: NEVEN TOMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: These are decisions, and they were reached as a result of the non-functioning of the Presidency of the HZ-HB which pertain to their authorities within the scope of the regulations that prevailed at the time.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Now, the second of the two items in that one paragraph is the proposal on the appointment of the HVO, Kresevo municipality. Does this confirm, sir, that it was within the power of the HVO HZ-HB to, in fact, appoint an entire municipal staff, in this case for Kresevo?

utterances.speaker: NEVEN TOMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I can remember, the situation was as I have already mentioned. Because of the non-functioning of the Presidency of the HZ-HB, this was taken over by the HVO HZ-HB, and the appointment of Kresevo municipality is hereby confirmed. I don't remember any other such decisions, because in practical terms presidents of the municipal HVO were members of the Presidency of the HZ-HB, i.e., they were our heads. Hence, the authority lie with the Presidency of the HZ-HB. However, since they could not be convened during this period, for organisational reasons, to organise the activities and implement regulations of the HZ-HB, this was a necessity, it had to be done.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Would you next go, please, to -- excuse me -- back to the Defence binder, 1D 01184. And this is, again, a set of minutes of the HVO meeting on the 9th of April, 1993, and again although there are a number of items covered in the document, I'd like to direct your attention to item number 9 on page 4 of the English translation, item 9. In item number 9, sir, there is discussion of a proposal to abrogate the decision on the mobilisation of material and technical equipment in the Mostar municipality. And if we skip the intervening paragraph, which although everyone will have it, the item 9 goes on to say: "Based on the above, a decision on the abrogation of the decision --" the referenced decision in Mostar municipality was unanimously adopted; correct?

utterances.speaker: NEVEN TOMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is about the non-competence of a municipality to carry out mobilisation according to the HZ-HB, and the HZ-HB department reacted to that, and the HVO HZ-HB confirmed the standpoint of the defence department and confirmed that it was contrary to the regulations of the HZ-HB.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Going back to -- or going to something, sir, which you've in fact mentioned several times in the last few minutes, and you were asked a number of questions during direct examination about the relationship between the HVO HZ-HB and the municipalities, the municipal HVOs, and if I understood your testimony correctly, sir, you indicated that one of the problems of controlling the HVO municipalities is because the HVO municipal presidents were members of the Presidency. But, sir, isn't it correct, as you've just said three or four times in the last 15 minutes, the HZ-HB Presidency wasn't functioning during this time; correct? There was no HZ-HB body to take up, if you will, the cause of these alleged recalcitrant HVOs because the Presidency wasn't meeting, was it? I think your word for the last few minutes has been because the HZ-HB Presidency was not functioning. Correct?

utterances.speaker: NEVEN TOMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The Presidency of the HZ-HB convened very seldom, and it did not function by way of calling meetings. Municipal presidents had contact with the president of the HZ-HB. The HVO of the HZ-HB, i.e., the municipal HVOs, did not publish Official Gazettes, so one could not follow what the municipalities were doing at the time, what regulations they were passing.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Sir, I think the evidence in this case establishes at this point and I would put to you that the evidence shows that between the end of August 1992 and late August 1993, that is, for one year, the HZ-HB Presidency, in fact, met twice, once on the 17th of October, 1992, and then, in fact, at the end of August or late August 1993, when the Croatian Republic of Herceg-Bosna was established. Now, during the interim time is it correct, sir, and do you agree with other witnesses, including such people as Mr. Buntic, that during that interim time when the Presidency was not meeting, the HVO HZ-HB was both executive and legislature and their laws, decrees and decisions had the force of law; correct?

utterances.speaker: NEVEN TOMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: And in terms any control of the HZ-HB Presidency when they did meet, which was rarely, please tell the Judges any time -- any instance in which the HZ-HB Presidency took any action to disapprove, veto or undo any action or decision taken by the HVO HZ-HB.

utterances.speaker: NEVEN TOMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Within the sphere of finance, there was a problem with the decree that regulated the payment of war tax on the part of workers working abroad. The municipal presidents, in practical terms, stopped the implementation of the decree that was passed by the HVO HZ-HB because they did not want that to be part of the budget of the HZ-HB, as the decree regulated.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues]... question.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: No, it was not.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: It was an open-ended question. Read the question, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Whoa, hold on.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: I'm not holding on. This is unfair. He asked, "Please explain to the Judges." He's explaining, he shouldn't be interrupted. I object to this tactic.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: I don't know why Mr. Karnavas is so alarmed. The question is on the page and it says: "In terms of any control of the HZ-HB Presidency, when they did meet, which was rarely, please tell the Judges any time -- any instance in which the HZ-HB Presidency took any action to disapprove, veto or undo any action or decision taken by the HVO HZ-HB."

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: My question had nothing to do with the dislike of some municipalities of what was happening. My question was: Name me, sir, and I repeat it again -- give me an instance when the HZ-HB Presidency, when in session, vetoed, disapproved, undid anything, anything that the HVO HZ-HB had done.

utterances.speaker: NEVEN TOMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The Presidency of the HZ-HB ratified the decisions passed by the HVO HZ-HB. However, I gave you an example, and this was the decree that the HVO HZ-HB passed, and that decree was not implemented in practice because members of the Presidency of the HZ-HB did not want to implement this decree, and they were at the same time heads of the municipalities, and they had legal power not to implement this decree, especially those municipalities that had a lot of workers working abroad, and it was not their goal for these revenues to be channeled towards the budget of the HVO HZ-HB. It was rather their intention and wish for that money to remain at the municipality level.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Sir, the answer to my question is: It never happened, it never happened, there was never a single occasion when the HZ-HB Presidency undid or vetoed anything that the HVO HZ-HB had done; correct? It never happened?

utterances.speaker: NEVEN TOMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not through official meetings. However, I gave you an example according to which a decree passed by the HVO HZ-HB that was not adopted or, rather, that it was not implemented in practice on the ground.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Sir, you testified last Tuesday: "All decisions taken by the HVO HZ-HB have been implemented." Now, are you changing your testimony?

utterances.speaker: NEVEN TOMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. Decisions that were adopted by the HVO HZ-HB were, indeed, implemented. Throughout all that time, we struggled for the decisions to be implemented, i.e., to be operational. I mentioned just one decision which was not implemented at all as a result of the work of the municipalities and their heads. As a result of all that, a compromise was reached and regulations were changed. Finally, it was part of the revenues of the municipalities rather than of the HZ-HB. Whatever regulations we passed, we made sure, as much as possible, for them to be implemented, and within that context I said that all the regulations and decisions that we reached were, indeed, implemented.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Sir, you were asked a number of questions last week about indicating that Mr. Boban, one of the hats that he wore, he was the president of the HZ-HB Presidency. Mr. Boban was no shrinking violet, was he? I'm not sure that will translate, but he was not an unforceable person in expressing his views; correct? He was not -- strike all of that. Sorry, my poor question. Sir, Mr. Boban was an active and forceful personality, wasn't he, or at least could be?

utterances.speaker: NEVEN TOMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: And as president of the HZ-HB, I take it any of these municipal HVO presidents could have taken their grievances to Mr. Boban at any time, or called him on the telephone, for that matter, in Herzegovina. Correct?

utterances.speaker: NEVEN TOMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: And, again, can you tell the Judges one occasion when Mate Boban intervened with the HVO HZ-HB to undo, veto, disapprove any action taken by the HVO HZ-HB?

utterances.speaker: NEVEN TOMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have to go back to the decree that I've just mentioned. After their objections to Mr. Boban and after their complaints, Mr. Boban called for the regulation to be changed and that the war tax become revenue of the municipalities that would be channeled towards the defence, in agreement with the defence department. That's how the decree was worded, and it was only then that it actually started being implemented in the territory of the HZ-HB.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: All right. I take that on board, sir, but let me come back to my question. Was there ever a time Mr. Boban communicated with the HVO HZ-HB, to your knowledge, called -- Mr. Prlic called you, came to a meeting, sent a representative to the meeting, and say, "At the last HVO HZ-HB meeting, you took this action. I don't like it. The municipal HVOs don't like it. I'm hereby saying you can't do it"? Did anything like that ever happen?

utterances.speaker: NEVEN TOMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: When was that?

utterances.speaker: NEVEN TOMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The example of the decree that I've just mentioned is an example of that.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Is that the only example you can think of?

utterances.speaker: NEVEN TOMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is an example pertaining to my sphere of work. That's why I remember it. But I know that he communicated individually with department heads and that he suggested certain solutions that they should adopt.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Well, I think eventually the Judges will probably have just about every HVO minute in the record for them to review, and the lawyers -- and all the lawyers can argue about that at some point, I suppose. If you remember, this afternoon I took you to Exhibit P00303, and in the interests of time I'm going to suggest we probably don't have to look at it. But if you remember, that was the clause that we stopped and looked at and said the Presidency of the HZ-HB shall appoint and dismiss the other members of the HVO HZ-HB. The Presidency of the HZ-HB had that power, and my question to you again, sir: Can you tell the Judges one instance where the HZ-HB Presidency exercised any power to remove a member of the HVO HZ-HB?

utterances.speaker: NEVEN TOMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: You can't -- again, sir, you can't remember one way or the other or you don't recall any occasion when that happened?

utterances.speaker: NEVEN TOMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't recall any such example.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Sir, in terms of your dealings with the HVO municipal governments, just to summarise this point, I put it to you, sir, if you had such a severe problem or such a problem as you've indicated to the Judges last week with any particular HVO municipal government, assuming for the moment that's correct, did you take any action -- did the HVO HZ-HB take any action available, send your laws, send your armies, send the police, and remove any of those governments or members of those governments who were disobedient to your administration?

utterances.speaker: NEVEN TOMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Last week, I spoke about letters that I sent to the president of the HZ-HB, to the municipal heads. I also had individual conversations with the municipal presidents, and I tried to implement the HZ-HB regulations. We have to bear in mind that the municipalities had built their own powers or authorities in their respective territories even before the establishment of the HVO HZ-HB, and they had real power on the ground. At the same time, the HVO HZ-HB did not have any instruments available to it to force them to do anything.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Sir, the HVO HZ-HB pursued policies and sent armies and police into the field to carry out that policy, including expulsions, including fights, taking over villages. You certainly did have power, sir. And are you telling the Judges that you did not have the ability to send the police, to send law enforcement, to send the military, if necessary, to gain control of some municipal official who you say would not get in line?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Your Honour, I'm going to object to the form of question. Now, unless he can establish the facts in this question, there are facts beyond -- you know, that are not in evidence. Where is it that the HVO HZ-HB sent armies into the field? Where does he get this? I mean, look at the question. It's loaded with facts. How does one answer "yes" or "no." I mean, let's be fair. I'm trying to be measured here, but let's be fair to the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Sir, the Judges, over the past two and a half years -- excuse me. I'm sorry, Mr. President. Sir, the Judges have heard evidence over the past two and a half years, and they'll of course ultimately decide. I'm not saying it's been established once and for all, but they've certainly heard an abundance of evidence indicating Muslim administrations in municipalities being removed and war presidencies being removed or displaced in a number of locations, Varos comes to mind at the moment, and I do put it to you, sir, that was being done by people who ultimately the HVO HZ-HB controlled. Bruno Stojic and the Department of Defence reported to the HVO HZ-HB. Now, if you could send the military and police to displace Muslim administrations and take out Muslim war presidencies, why couldn't you get one recalcitrant HVO municipal official in line?

utterances.speaker: NEVEN TOMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know -- I'm not sure that I understood your question correctly. However, our task was to organise the civilian life in the territory of the HZ-HB and to build a system for the survival during that period. Those were the priorities of both my department and the HZ-HB. In other words, we were mostly concerned with the implementation of our own rules, the rules and regulations that we, ourselves, had passed.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Sir, if you could go next to Exhibit in the Defence binder, please, 1D 02357. This is an article of an interview with Mr. Prlic on the 25th of January, 1992. There's a translation error on the date. I'm sure the original can be seen to be "1992." Sir, on page 2 of the English version, but in the -- it would be -- there's a question that's put to Mr. Prlic that said: "Is a BH currency the solution?" And obviously I'm changing topics now to a part of your testimony dealing with currency, the BH dinar, the Croatian dinar, the Deutsche mark. On this particular occasion, under that question: "Is a BH currency a solution," at the end of his answer Mr. Prlic says: "The problem is, therefore, how in this situation to introduce a new currency which the largest part of the republic would not recognise." "Question: What parts are you referring to? "Answer: "In the SAO, the Serbian autonomous areas or Krajinas, they want the Serbian dinar, in Western Herzegovina the Croatian one." Isn't it true, sir, that long before there was any discussion of introduction of the BH dinar, which didn't take place until September/October of 1992, some months later, it was already clear the Serbs wanted the Yugoslav dinar and many of the Croats, at least in Western Herzegovina, they wanted the Croatian currency; correct? That's what Mr. Prlic says, and I guess I'll put it to you. Do you agree or disagree with Mr. Prlic?

utterances.speaker: NEVEN TOMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The fundamental issue of money is also the issue of trust or confidence in the currency and in the institution that stands behind that currency, which is the Central bank. The confidence in the Central bank stems from the confidence in the state. Under such circumstances, it was, at that time if 1992, there were no preconditions to build confidence in a currency that would be introduced which would also prove to be true after its introduction.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: I apologise, I apologise for interrupting. My question is much simpler, and that is: Do you agree or disagree with Mr. Prlic that it was already clear that the largest part of the republic would not recognise a new currency; the Serbs wanted the Serbian dinar, and in Western Herzegovina the Croats wanted the Croatian dinar? Now, that was what Mr. Prlic said. Do you agree or disagree?

utterances.speaker: NEVEN TOMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: You disagree?

utterances.speaker: NEVEN TOMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I disagree.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: And in this article, there is a reference -- in fact, the article is titled: "Looting On Both Sides." Is it true that around this time in the latter part of 1991, Croatia was trucking large amounts of Yugoslav dinars to Bosnia-Herzegovina?

utterances.speaker: NEVEN TOMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, at that period of time a lot of Jugo dinars appeared in Bosnia-Herzegovina. Some came from Yugoslavia, some from Croatia.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Above the part that I read to you a moment ago, above the question: "Is a BH currency the solution," Mr. Prlic says: "If it is true that large amounts of money have been transferred from Croatia, that then means that we have been robbed by the West as well." So I come back to my question, sir. Is it correct that Croatia at that time was trucking large amounts of Yugoslav dinars into Bosnia?

utterances.speaker: NEVEN TOMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: And was that some deliberate attempt to sabotage the BH economy, the Bosnian economy, or why send all this currency, which Croatia apparently doesn't want, into Bosnia-Herzegovina?

utterances.speaker: NEVEN TOMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This money had no value in the Republic of Croatia. It was earmarked for municipalities in Herzegovina which could still exchange the money for German marks or buy goods with the money. By exchanging those funds, the municipalities obtained revenue, and you can see that this revenue was subsequently used for defence.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Before we move on from this document, sir, if I can go up to the first question that is put to Mr. Prlic in this article, and it says: "Mr. Prlic, why are you avoiding questions about politics when today everything boils down to politics?" "Answer: Precisely because everything boils down to politics, or better to put it, to politicking, in other words --i.e., in other words, to the ethnic field." Do you agree, sir, that by 25 January 1992, the predominant factor in what was happening in the former Yugoslavia was politics and ethnic politics at that? And once again my question really is: Do you agree with Mr. Prlic's assessment?

utterances.speaker: NEVEN TOMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: And, sir, didn't that really ultimately have more to do with Herceg-Bosna's selection of the Croatian dinar than any sort of monetary or financial reasons? Herceg-Bosna chose the Croatian dinar because ethnic -- primarily for ethnic reasons and its affiliation or desired affiliation with the Republic of Croatia; isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: NEVEN TOMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's not correct, no. The municipalities introduced the Croatian dinar on an individual basis. It depended on the arrival of goods and on the possibility of obtaining new goods. I've already mentioned in my testimony that the municipality of Jablanica adopted such a decision, as well as other municipalities, and the HVO HZ-HB issued a decree regulating that salaries should be paid in Croatian dinars. They didn't introduce the Croatian dinar because the Croatian dinar was already being used, as was the case for the German mark.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Let's go to another article by Mr. Prlic about 15 months later, which is 1D 02222 in the Defence binder, the binder you're just been in, so it shouldn't be too difficult. 1D 02222, and this is an article by Mr. Prlic in Slobodna Dalmatija on the 29th of April, 1993, in which he writes about the introduction of the BH dinar. In one of the parts of his -- in fact, the first part of the bold language, under the bold language it says that one of the problems was a huge amount, as much as a third -- strike that -- that a huge amount of the BH dinars, as they were introduced, wound up, if you will, in the wrong hands. Did that happen in Herceg-Bosna as well or was somehow Herceg-Bosna immune from that situation?

utterances.speaker: NEVEN TOMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In the course of my testimony, I explained how we directed Bosnian and Herzegovinian dinars into municipalities in Central Bosnia, because you could obtain goods and equipment and pay with this currency, because in that area the BH dinar was accepted, and you know the main bills of all companies and of legal entities were in BH dinars. So with reference to BH dinars, there never was embezzlement of any kind.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: In the -- under the bold heading, not counting that one, but in the paragraphs that follow, and I'm trying to just give you a point of reference, in the fourth paragraph under there -- under that, excuse me, and for the English readers, bottom of page 1 in the translation,

utterances.speaker: MR. PRLIC SAYS
utterances.text: "There was no obstruction to the introduction of this currency in the territory of the Croatian Community of Herceg-Bosna," et cetera, "but there was obstruction to the realistic assessment of the entire undertaking." Now, in contrast to that, sir, let me just put it to you, what Mr. Prlic says, there was no obstruction, hadn't Herceg-Bosna by that time made it very clear that it was seeking to establish a Croatian space? I think, in fact, the term that was maybe used by others was a single economic space. But by this time, Herceg-Bosna and its leadership had made it very clear, had it not, it was attempting to carve out a Croatian space in Bosnia and Herzegovina, at least for a time; correct? And wasn't it fully part of that to adopt and use the Croatian currency as opposed to some other currency?

utterances.speaker: NEVEN TOMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I have to say that that's wrong, because Herceg-Bosna, the Croatian Community of Herceg-Bosna, also included areas inhabited by Croats, areas in which the BH dinar was also a currency. Sarajevo and other areas. This was an attempt to establish a system that would protect the Croats in those areas and create the economic preconditions to assist certain parts, so that's why the Croatian dinar wasn't what was used to make such assessments. The Croatian dinar arrived in a natural way with goods and with people who received aid in Croatian dinars when they were refugees. Medhamed [phoen], the Muslim charity, gave people money that they received from foreign donators in German marks, but in Croatia people had to change -- exchange that money, because only Croatian dinars were used there. So with those Croatian dinars, they would come and buy goods, and that's why the Croatian dinar disappeared from the market later on, because there was no -- there were no more goods.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues]... part of this article, sorry, but we have to move on. On the next-to-last paragraph of Mr. Prlic's article, he seems to indicate that there were three other avenues that could have been pursued -- could have been prevented. He says: "The discrediting of the state could have been prevented in several ways; by payments in convertible currency," first, so it stopped there. Can you tell the Judges what is -- tell me and tell everyone, what's a convertible currency?

utterances.speaker: NEVEN TOMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, the German mark is what one has in mind, or the American US dollar. These are currencies that were listed by banks as currencies that could be exchanged.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Mr. Prlic goes on to say the second thing that could have been done is the issue of coupons in certain areas. But as I understood your testimony last week, sir, you were critical of coupons, and yet here Mr. Prlic seems to be recommending that as one course of action, at least in some areas. Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: NEVEN TOMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Do you agree or disagree with Mr. Prlic?

utterances.speaker: NEVEN TOMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, one's talking about issuing coupons in certain areas where it was possible to control how this money was used and where it was possible to control its value. I said that the BH dinar, the Bosnian and Herzegovinian dinar, which was supposed to be issued throughout the state, was converted into coupons that had various values in Tuzla, Zenica and Sarajevo, so whoever administers this money makes it possible to carry out looting. One can shift money from one area to another. I understand the suggestion coupons could be used in a certain area if there was supervision, protection. In such areas, such coupons could have a stable value. One could trust the way in which such coupons were used and people wouldn't fear their money disappearing.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: And the third option which Mr. Prlic lists here is officially introducing the Croatian dinar, and we'll continue on that when -- of course as we go.

utterances.speaker: NEVEN TOMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Here a possibility is mentioned. One could pay in cash, and that was the case in a large swathe of the free territory.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Before we leave this document, in the last paragraph it makes reference to an agreement on payment transactions between these states, referring to the Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina and the Republic of Croatia. Can you tell the Judges, please, what sort of agreement on payment transactions existed at that time between Bosnia and Croatia?

utterances.speaker: NEVEN TOMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: At the time, there were agreements between Bosnia and Herzegovina and Croatia and Bosnia and Herzegovina and Slovenia, agreements on payment transactions and using non-resident accounts.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Let's go next to 1D 01350. 1D 01350. And just to confirm, do you agree that this is the confirmation of the receipt by Herceg-Bosna authorities of approximately three billion BH dinars in connection with the initial distribution or introduction of that currency?

utterances.speaker: NEVEN TOMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: And I just had one additional question about that document. It says, item 14 the costs of delivery, unloading, placing in the vaults, loading, the transfer of workers and record-keeping expenses amounts to 46 million BH dinars. So who got that money, who got 46 million dinars?

utterances.speaker: NEVEN TOMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: People who came from Central Bosnia received this money.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: No, no, sir. My question is specifically the 46 million in costs. The item 14 talks about costs, which is taken out of the gross amount, and I'm just asking, if you can assist us: Who received the 46 million BH dinars?

utterances.speaker: NEVEN TOMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Workers of the municipal HVOs from Central Bosnia received this money. It was to cover their expenses, the expenses of coming there, fuel, accommodation, et cetera. So it was these people who physically transported the money and took it to Central Bosnia who received this money.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues]... tied this back into further in your testimony last week, when you indicated that approximately a third of the currency had been -- well, I'm not sure exactly which word you used at the time, but basically a third of the currency had been seized or taken by Herceg-Bosna to make sure kind of they'd get their share. Now, again, are we talking about essentially the same transaction here, same event, as reflected in this document?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Your Honour, the word "seize" has been used. Perhaps we could have a page reference to where in the transcript Mr. Tomic said that the money was seized, meaning stolen.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Well, not stolen, but I think -- well, let me ask the witness this. Maybe I misunderstood.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Sir, you testified last week that there was several trucks of currency were sent to Herceg-Bosna. Apparently you're now saying these were people from Central Bosnia who then bore the cost of doing so and that about a third of this money then was kept -- strike the word "seized," was then kept with these three trucks in Herceg-Bosna. Now, is that what happened or did I misunderstand your testimony?

utterances.speaker: NEVEN TOMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think you misunderstood my testimony. A representative of the government of the Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina is responsible for transporting money from the printers to Celije in Bosnia and Herzegovina, and this person decided that this lorry should remain in the territory of the HZ-HB, whereas the other two lorries continued on their way to Central Bosnia. We obtained this money in accordance with what he was competent for, and we used it in the most efficient way possible at the time, in terms of maintaining the value of the money received. So nothing was actually seized.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: I strike the word "seized." I think -- well, we can go back on the record if we need to last week. You received one of the trucks, one of the lorries, and the money as indicated on 1D 01350 was received. Now, I notice this introduction, according to this report, was on the 15th of October, 1992. Correct?

utterances.speaker: NEVEN TOMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: If you can work with me before finish the evening. If you can look next, please, in the first binder to Exhibit P00447. The first Prosecution binder, P00447. If you can just confirm for me, sir, is this a decree issued on the 22nd of September, 1992, by the HVO HZ-HB titled: "On the Regulation of Payment Transaction in Croatian Dinars on the Territory of the Croatian Community of Herceg-Bosna"?

utterances.speaker: NEVEN TOMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that is the decree that regulates payment transactions in Croatian dinars.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: As the head of the finance department of the HVO at that time, I take it you would have been involved, probably, in drafting or otherwise preparing this decree. Would that be fair to say?

utterances.speaker: NEVEN TOMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Your Honour, I'm going to suggest that might be a time to stop, before we go to the next document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] My colleague Judge Prandler is telling me that on line 25, page 87, there is mention of territories. Is that the adequate term?

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Sorry, Mr. President, are you directing that question to me or to the witness?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: [French spoken].

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: If you can assist us, Mr. Tomic, please.

utterances.speaker: NEVEN TOMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Can you just remind me which part you're referring to?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Witness, please, in this decree there is mention of territories of the Croat Community of Herceg-Bosna. What did this mean, exactly?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very often at the beginning of the HVO HZ-HB, the term "area" or "territory" would be used. The term "territory" was used when copying the provisions that regulated situations in the territory of Yugoslavia, so it has to do with the area of the HZ-HB, the area covered in the decision on establishing the HZ-HB.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. It is 7.00 p.m. I believe it is time to adjourn. We will be sitting tomorrow at 2.15 p.m. As I told you, I will be at the door at 2.14, so I'll see you tomorrow for tomorrow's hearing.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Tuesday, the 4th day of November, 2008, at 2.15 p.m. 25

procedural_notes.text: --- Whereupon the hearing adjourned at 7.01 p.m.,
